For a good and considerable time now, many excellent and highly learned people have diligently pursued this <term>Spagyric Art<note>The term "Spagyric" refers to alchemical techniques—specifically the process of separating, purifying, and then recombining the essential components of a substance to create medicine.</note></term>, publicly and in writing commending, lauding, and highly praising it for its high and excellent utility in **medicine** and the <note>original: *cura morborum*</note> cure of diseases—to say nothing of the **transmutation** of metals. They have demonstrated its <note>original: *Veritatem, Antiquitatem und Utilitatē*</note> truth, antiquity, and utility through excellent commendations and other writings, and by publishing many good and select *chemical booklets* by Bernhard <note>Referring to Bernhard of Trevisan, a legendary 15th-century alchemist.</note> and other excellent philosophers. For a good and lengthy time now, many excellent and highly learned people have diligently pursued this <term>Spagyric Art<note>A branch of alchemy focused on medicine, specifically the process of separating, purifying, and recombining the components of natural substances to create potent remedies.</note></term>, publicly and in writing commending, glorifying, and highly praising it for its high and excellent utility in **Medicine** and the **cure of diseases** <note>original: *cura morborum*</note>, to say nothing of the **transmutation** of metals.

# Of the Preparation <note>original: *De præparatione*</note> 34

The Philosophical Gold—that is, the Tincture or <term>Quintessence</term> <note>the "Fifth Essence," the purest and most potent spiritual core of a substance</note> of Gold—is the beginning and father of all metals, and it has no need for any of them. But they all have need of it, for this reason: just as man was first created entirely beautiful and magnificent, but through the **Fall** <note>referring to the biblical Fall of Man, which introduced death and corruption into the world</note> became darkened and mortal, and therefore all his children also became mortal and thus stood in great need of a Savior; so also were all metals, from their first beginning, created entirely beautiful and indestructible through their father—that is, the Tinctures which are locked within gold. *Add examples* <note>original: *Adde exempla*</note> from the ancient **War of the Knights** <note>referring to *The Ancient War of the Knights* (*Der Uralte Ritter-Krieg*), a famous alchemical allegory depicting the struggle between different metallic principles</note>. Because their mother, the Queen, [pursued] foreign love—that is, she did not remain in her first state, but became defiled through the movement of the elements. Therefore, their bodies were made subject to perishability, though some more than others.

After the mother had defiled herself and her <term>Elements</term> had entered into a state of inequality, they could be ignited by a poor, accidental fire and burn their own body. Thus, the Luciferian, impure, and foreign <term>Sulfur</term> <note>in alchemy, "Sulfur" represents the active, combustible, and masculine principle of a substance</note>—taken on within the mother—ignites its <term>Body</term> <note>original: *Corpus*</note>, burns it, and thereafter separates the soul (which was poured into it by the father of the Philosophical Suns in the first movement) and sacrifices it to the air. ### BERNHARDI

...so that we, together with him, become one heart, victorious over all our enemies forever and eternally. # Of the First Matter
<note>original: "de Materia prima"</note>

God in the Holy Trinity—as God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—knows all things together because of their actual, inexpressible, great mysteries and secrets <note>original: "Arcana"</note>, from which the heavenly and earthly creation and art of almighty God is to be seen. Our ancestors and philosophers <note>original: "Philosophi"</note> have learned and discovered the art of alchemy <note>original: "Alchymen"</note> from this single matter. What this our matter is in its hidden nature—what it has, can, and is able to do—I cannot sufficiently write of, report, tell, laud, honor, and praise. For it is worthy of all honor; it is held in great honor and dignity by those of both high and low station, especially by the philosophers, and also by those who obtain grace from God and understand the knowledge of this nature. It is the Sun <note>original: "Sol," representing gold or the masculine principle</note> and Moon <note>original: "Luna," representing silver or the feminine principle</note>, man and woman, indeed everything. It is despised, swallowed, and trodden underfoot; it is present in love and sorrow. And when it putrefies, it is to be compared to a stinking carcass, a dragon, and a raven because of the foul stench it takes on. It is also a wonder that out of such a matter, a pleasant, beautiful, joyful flower and secret <note>original: "Secret"</note> is brought forth through the philosophical art, as I have truly discovered through my own labor <note>original: "Laboriren," referring to practical laboratory work</note>, as you shall hear in my process <note>original: "Proceß," the specific set of chemical instructions</note> and thereafter further from the report, as follows.

[...through the] **philosophical vaporous fire**) is changed into something better and higher / it lays aside the mourning garment / which is then stained with its tears / in the form of a **black eagle**, **raven**, or **dragon**, bespattered with blood / which bathes out the fire: That is / when he must die / then he opens his mouth wide from the heat / so that **white wild doves** fly out of him / that is / the true **Philosophical Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*; the liquid or volatile principle in alchemy, symbolizing transformation.</note> / or the **Glue of the Eagle** <note>original: *Gluten Aquilæ*</note> / the movable / hidden / invisible / great actual nature / the beautiful clear **Queen** / clothed in her silver robe / which is spiritual / and has hidden within her the red robe and red collar of the **King** / as her husband.

When it has now been bathed white / and has laid aside its mourning and black garment / then the Queen is brought to him / she puts the joyful red garment on him / and sets a new golden crown upon his head / which is the true **Philosophical Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*; the active, solar, or soul principle in alchemy.</note> / **Soul** and **Spirit** / by which the King is awakened from death / and stands up through her and with her. Through such addition / marriage / and enclosure / they are united into a single **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> / having become so much more heartfelt / pure / clarified / and exalted / which is a penetrator and overcomer of all things / and thus **Soul**, **Spirit**, and **Body** <note>original: *Anima, Spiritus & Corpus*</note> remain together united and unharmed / and you are to rejoice in their flesh and blood. For this is the true / single / valiant Hero and Warrior / who has overcome his enemies through suffering / and thereby attains the fiery-cutting sword and **Tincture** <note>The "Tincture" or "Stone" is the final, potent substance capable of transforming other materials.</note> / which [gives] to the dead / unready **Minerals**, **Metals**, and **Plants** <note>original: *Vegetabilibus*</note> their strength / health / and life.

# Process of the Alchemical Art.

Hail, beautiful radiance of the Heavens, radiant light of the world! When this is coupled with the Moon, it becomes a marital union and a conjunction of Mercury. From these three—especially through the riverbed <note>original: *fluminis alveolum*, here used as a metaphor for the channel of "concupiscence" or intense desire/attraction</note> (the desire)—is born that strong giant, whom thousands upon thousands seek through the mastery of the art. When these things are thus dissolved—not in rainwater <note>original: *aqua nubis*, literally "water of the cloud"</note>—our gum is never purified; rather, our Gum (that is, the Body which is dissolved) is resolved into Mercurial (Spiritual) water. This blessed Gum of ours (that is, the Body or Water of Life), having been dissolved by itself as was said, now bears the name "Sperm of the Philosophers" (that is: salts are the roots of our work). <note>The "Sperm of the Philosophers" refers to the essential seed or creative principle extracted from the base matter.</note> Now it seeks to be coupled with the virgin, to be betrothed to the bride, and to make her pregnant in the Bath through the tempering of the fire (the "Bride," that is, the Quintessence). But the virgin is not impregnated suddenly, unless she is given a kiss through frequent embraces. Then conception takes place in the Womb, and thus a happy birth is brought forth in the order of nature.

Then, at the bottom of the vessel, there appears a strong Ethiopian <term>Ethiopian: *Æthiops* is the traditional alchemical term for the *nigredo* or "black stage," where the matter undergoes a symbolic death and putrefaction before being reborn.</term>, burnt, calcined, discolored in hue, utterly dead, and lacking life. Now he asks to be buried <gloss>He now asks for one thing, and desires to be buried</gloss> and to be raised up by his own moisture (that is, to lift himself up by his own liquid <gloss>to rise up again</gloss>) and to be gently calcined by the fire until, from the strength of the fire, he appears most white. But first he takes a drink by himself; through the perseverance of the fire, he now becomes well-washed by himself. Now he is made pleasing, reborn by his own sweat, and the body which was previously darkened is returned to a whitened state: Behold, the wondrous renewal of the Ethiopian! Henceforth he claims for himself a new name through the bath of regeneration, which the Philosophers call the "Sulphur of Nature" and their "Son," who is the Philosopher's Stone. But he is hidden from the foolish through their ignorance of natural philosophy—those who are deceived by the various resistances of the fire.

## ARTEPHIUS ON THE SECRETS
->of Nature.<-

He taught the way to make the Philosophers' Stone for the production of gold such that it is neither combustible nor composed of combustible things; its operation is easy, if you are able to ascend to the heights. # OF RAYMUND LULL
## Treatise on the Philosopher’s Stone, etc.

In the name of God, understand, hear, mark, and perceive—you, my most beloved friends—the surpassing, highest secret, which exceeds all the treasures of this entire world; which God gives to His elect and withholds from the ignorant. Therefore, if you wish to reach this secret, which God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit has poured into you, see to it that you first seek the Kingdom of God and His righteousness; then this gift shall be granted to you, and you will be gladdened to see the wonderful power that God has allowed into nature through its works.

In all growing things that are born in the earth, in the water, and above the earth, in the air and in the fire, the first movement is the Sun <note>original: "SOL"; in alchemy, the Sun represents both the celestial body and the terrestrial metal, Gold, as the source of vital heat.</note>, although nothing may be born nor destroyed without the four elements—namely heat, cold, dryness, and moisture—which nature serves. From nature, many a wonderful shape is born and formed according to the influence of the planets, whose image is impressed upon them; truly from another perspective, yet according to the quality of their temperament <term>complexion</term> <note>original: "Complexion"; a technical term in medieval science referring to the specific balance of the four humors or elements within a person or substance.</note>. For we see that in some things the four elements <term>Elementa</term> are in such equilibrium that no one element has power to rule over the others in its temperament <term>complexion</term>, as is found in pure Gold <note>original: "SOLE"; referring to the solar metal, gold, considered the most balanced and "perfect" substance.</note>; and these we call healthy and perfect bodies <term>CORPORA</term>. But in some things they are divided and are consumed in the exercise of their dominance, but more so in Mars <note>original: "Marte"; the planet and its corresponding metal, Iron.</note> and—

their dissolution <note>original: *Solutio*</note>, putrefaction <note>original: *Putrefactio*</note>, coagulation <note>original: *Coagulatio*</note>, distillation <note>original: *Destillatio*</note>, fixation <note>original: *Fixatio*</note>, and all the operations <note>original: *Werck*</note> which occur in one vessel <note>original: *Vase*</note>, for gold <note>original: *Sole*, literally "the Sun"</note> and silver <note>original: *Luna*, literally "the Moon"</note>, and from one single matter, as will be revealed hereafter. 

But some thought they must have water <note>original: *Aquam*</note> and oil <note>original: *Oleum*</note> to make the "earth" white <note>In alchemy, "whitening the earth" refers to a specific stage of purification</note>, and were diligent with the fire; and though these substances remained, they were of no use. For it is the nature of a collective moisture to cling kindly to bodies, just like our own moisture, which has water <note>original: *Aquam*</note>, oil <note>original: *Oleum*</note>, fire, and wax all within it, and acts as the medium between that which is fixed and that which is unfixed <note>Referring to the volatile and stable aspects of a substance</note>. 

But if they say that many stones—such as crystals <note>original: *Christallen*</note>, and lapis lazuli <note>original: *Lapis Lazuli*</note>, and other pearls <note>original: *Margariten*</note>, as well as certain stones of ore—are brought together by the four elements <note>original: *4. Elementen*</note> and thereby serve Nature: To this I say, even if these were heated with a sharp fire, their moisture would remain unconsumed; for they see well that no moisture left them during their distillation, and they become a composite. 

In the same way, they might well lay the elements <note>original: *Elementa*</note> together, coagulate them, and make them stable: since they serve Nature, and they would not do it unless Nature itself did it. But hear the philosophers <note>original: *Philosophos*</note>, who say that a proper birth <note>The natural generation of minerals within the earth</note> hardly occurs in a thousand years: And even if a person recognized Nature in heat and moisture, in cold and dryness, still such a substance that would be good for our Work could not be produced in a hundred years. 

For there is something else in Nature. Her working sometimes requires that no heat come to it for a long time, yet our Work is always with heat. Therefore the philosophers <note>original: *Philosophos*</note> call our stone a Salamander <note>A mythical creature believed to live in and endure fire; here, it symbolizes the alchemical substance that remains stable and is "nourished" by intense heat</note>, because it is fed by fire alone.

### Treatise of Llull
<note>Header original: *LULLII Tractat*; referring to Ramon Llull, a 13th-century philosopher to whom many alchemical works were later attributed.</note>

...can do. For whatever is divided by Nature always demands its own specific property; but whatever is undivided seeks its own nature as well. Therefore, things that are divisible—or have been divided—cannot create an eternal thing; but those which are indivisible and made eternal can also create their own kind. Just as all births produce their own likeness: the eternal God has made all human souls eternal, which is the reason they are formed in His likeness. But as far as the outward form is concerned, these have emerged from natural movements, which are all perishable. For as soon as they are dissolved <note>original: *solvirt*; to break a substance down into its components</note> and destroyed, they never return to their original constitution <term>Complexion: the specific balance of the four qualities—hot, cold, moist, and dry—that gives a body its unique character</term>. And this is easily seen in plants <note>original: *Vegetabilibus*</note>, birds, and fish; for they are all destructible and subject to death. It is exactly the same in this Art.

But if they say that imperfect bodies are also divided and destroyed, then brought back to their nature, and that Gold <note>original: *Sol*</note> and Silver <note>original: *Luna*</note> are made from them: To this we say that our Art does this, and not Nature alone. For even if the Art were to lie eternally within imperfect bodies <note>original: *imperfectis corporibus*; base metals such as lead, tin, or copper</note>, Nature could create neither Gold nor Silver there without the assistance of this Art. And whoever does not know this is in error.

For all such things that must be saturated with water or oil possess the nature of salt, alum, and glass, as was written before; they do not possess such a moisture as our moisture is,

# LULLY'S Treatise
Sig: Es

...neither water, nor any kind of thing. Rather, that you add its ***Tincture*** <note>original: "Tinctur"; in alchemy, a "tincture" is a potent substance or essence capable of transmuting or coloring other materials.</note> to it, as is written hereafter. For it is a ***Substance*** that becomes white and red of its own accord. But so that you do not scold us, we reveal the secret entirely, so that you may understand all the works of the <term>Philosophers</term> <note>The "Philosophers" refers to alchemists, who called their practice the "Hermetic Philosophy."</note>.

Firstly, the fixed (that is, the intermediate nature) is ***dissolved*** <note>original: "solvirt"</note> in its mother, who is not fixed; however, this happens in no other way than that they are bound closely together in a short vessel, where they may not escape one another, and are tormented with fire. Then each acts upon the other and they become one thing, as they were before; and thus they struggle with the enemies, and the coarse material grows and rises up into the highest places. Therefore, guard it well so that it is not lost; and thus the highest fixed thing becomes unfixed. 

Then it is properly called ***dissolved*** <note>original: "solvirt"</note>, and quite soon the heat produces blackness, and that is its ***putrefaction*** <note>original: "Fäulung"; the "nigredo" or black stage, symbolizing the death of the old form before rebirth.</note>, and it is an internal ***Solution*** of which the ***Philosophers*** write. And it is a key to this whole art: it can neither give birth nor be destroyed unless it undergoes putrefaction; there the white grain has died and brings forth a hundredfold fruit, and from there it rises from the earth into heaven, and from heaven back down to the earth. And that which is bodily becomes spiritual in sublimation, and that which is spiritual becomes bodily in the descent, and it has the power of the highest ***element***. Understand it thus: When the ***solution*** occurs and now the strong ignition happens, it circles around in the vessel like boiling water; thus the body is as much above as it is below. For nature leaves no empty space between, and that is its ***distillation*** and ***sublimation***.

### Concerning the Philosopher's Stone.

Some believe that the ***Elixir*** must be sublimated <note>Sublimation in alchemy involves heating a substance until it turns to vapor, then collecting the purified solid that forms upon cooling.</note>, but this is not the case; for they would not attain the mastery of the <term>Philosophers</term> nor their true meaning. Instead, after a long period of waiting <note>original: "Harung"; meaning to abide or persist in a state.</note> and constant cooking in the fire, it becomes fixed. This is its <term>calcination</term> <note>The process of reducing a substance to a powder through heat.</note> and <term>coagulation</term> <note>The thickening or solidification of a liquid substance.</note>, and it thus gives birth to White in the dry, and Yellow in the white, and Red in the yellow, as was said before. 

Between the black and the white colors, all the colors that the human mind can imagine will appear. However, these are not to be heeded, as they are not permanent, until the true Whiteness arrives. That is the truest ***ELIXIR***, composed of transparent things. For when it becomes an ***ELIXIR***, it is visible—indeed, more than visible—like the color of a pure mirror-glass, heavenly; and it becomes gentle in human trials through the aforementioned Whiteness.

And so the work ends in three times 40 days, each stage lasting 40 days. In the first 40 days, the Male <note>Symbolizing the active principle, often associated with sulfur.</note> rules, and his seed <note>original: "Sperma"</note> unites with the Female <note>Symbolizing the passive principle, often associated with mercury.</note>, never to be parted from each other eternally. In the second 40 days, it is formed and receives the Soul, the Spirit, and the ***Tincture***, and it becomes living. In the third 40 days, the pure fruit is born, to which nothing is equal. It becomes fusible and fluid, and through its fiery spirit, it no longer fears the fire; rather, it rests in the fire comfortably, and shall thus rule over all the treasures of the whole world. For it keeps bodies healthy and heals all sicknesses <note>original: "Siechtagen"</note>, whether they be of a hot or cold nature. And were it not for the natural death ordained by God, it would make bodies eternal, because of its eternal and balanced elements.

In his final hour of death, all four <note>Referring to the four classical elements: earth, water, air, and fire, which were believed to compose the human body.</note> are separated from him again, and each thing that is elemental in man returns to its element or matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> from which it was taken. ### THE DIALOGUE BEGINS, etc. <note>original Latin: "INCIPIT COLLOQUIUM"</note>

I, *Xamolxides*, traveled through many cities/ and always asked after such people/ who were experienced in Nature/ and from youth onward had applied themselves to **alchemy** <note>original: "Alchymey"</note>/ and other arts/ as I then found them in all places/ but few/ who had stepped toward the right **foundation** <note>original Latin: "Fundament"</note>. Although some had the gift from the **gods** <note>original Latin: "Diis"</note>/ it did not seem fitting for my person (who was not yet **perfect** and complete in spirit) to ask such secrets from them.

# Philosophical Gateway <note>original Latin: "Dyrrachium Philosophicum." Dyrrachium was an ancient Adriatic port, here used metaphorically as a gateway or entry point to philosophical knowledge.</note>

Al-Kindi <note>referring to a specific alchemical text attributed to the philosopher Al-Kindi</note>, though it is small, yet it is adorned with great secrets; I took pleasure in it and studied it for several years by calling upon my God, yet I could not understand it or interpret it with my spirit. I summoned many **spirits** <note>original Latin: "Spiritus"</note> for this purpose, who were meant to instruct me so that I might understand it. But it was always refused me by them; perhaps they themselves knew nothing of this **Gift** <note>original Latin: "Dono"</note>, though in my understanding they should have been **all-knowing** <note>original Latin: "omniscii"</note>. Or perhaps I was not yet worthy at that time, because I was still a child of the world and sometimes obedient to the goddess **Venus** <note>The text uses the symbol ♀ for Venus, here implying earthly lusts or worldly distractions.</note>.

In my old age, when I reached the total of 50 years and had practiced well in **natural philosophy** <note>original Latin: "Philosophia naturali"; the study of nature and the physical universe, a precursor to modern science.</note>, I once went out according to my old custom into a field to meditate. I came upon a beautiful, pleasant meadow by the mountain called **GRACE** <note>original Latin: "GRATIAE"</note> and sat down by the **Fountain of Grace** which flowed out of the mountain. Because I was very weary from the heat and had found no sleep in my eyes for three days and nights, I fell into a slumber there. I had many strange dreams and dealings with spirits, since from my youth I had practiced more in spiritual matters than in worldly things.

However, after I awoke, a **pygmy** <note>original Latin: "Pygmæus"; in alchemical tradition, these were often "gnomes" or earth-spirits who guarded minerals and secrets within mountains.</note> was sitting by me at the fountain in blue clothes and with a long beard, at which I was terrified. At last, I asked what he was doing there. He gave me a wise and intelligible answer and spoke: "My Xamolxides, I am sent by Queen **AURELIA** <note>Latin for "Golden One"; a personification of the alchemical goal or the refined substance of the Great Work.</note> to ask you what you are philosophizing about."

**XAMOLXIDES.** Upon these words, I reflected for a long time on how to answer, for I noticed that he was a **mountain-man** <note>original German: "Bergmännlein"; a legendary mine-dwelling spirit or gnome common in German folklore.</note>. Finally, we came to a locked palace, which was well-guarded by two strong lions. But when we approached, Peliel struck the lions with the hazel rod, and they fell silent...

If a person is strong and in middle age, take a piece the size of a pea and divide your medicine into [the size of] barleycorns, like other **Philosophers** <note>the "Philosophers by Fire," or alchemists</note>; give a child half a barleycorn or a whole one, according to the person’s constitution. The Dialogue of Albert Bayrs

# DIALOGUE OF THE SPIRIT
## OF MERCURY, WITH BROTHER ALBERT BAYRS Of the Carmelite Order, etc.

->SPIRIT OF MERCURY.<-

What is the reason that you have bewitched and bound <note>original: "gebannet"; to bind or constrain a spirit through ritual magic</note> me with so much idolatry and conjurations <note>original: "Conjurationibus"; Latin for formal incantations used in ritual magic</note>?

->ALBERT.<-

I will tell you the reason, if you will first assure me against danger to my body and life, and to my soul.

->SPIRIT.<-

That is not within my power; however, I have not come to do such things to you. But if you will not cease your sorcery, you are already assigned to another, who will well know how to carry out the execution <note>original: "Execution"; referring to the carrying out of a judicial or divine sentence</note> upon you and those of your kind. Regarding the salvation of your soul, I can neither hinder nor help you; yet, if I were a human, I would certainly wish to be saved. Therefore, answer my question.

->ALBERT.<-

## ALBERTUS.

I, Brother Albert Bayr, of the Carmelite Order <note>original: *Ordinis Carmelitani*. The Carmelites are a Catholic mendicant order.</note>, hereby swear and testify before God and His angels and dear saints, that in the year 1568, on the 18th day of February—which was the feast of the glorious and highly blessed, eternal Virgin Mary, Candlemas <note>Candlemas (February 2nd/18th depending on the calendar used) commemorates the presentation of Jesus at the Temple; it is a significant day in the liturgical and folk calendar.</note>—as I was in my cell in the monastery, Mary Magdalene of the New Star <note>original: *Maria Magdalena de Stella nova*.</note>, such a vision appeared to me and held the aforementioned dialogue with me. After I had risen and gone to bed day and night with philosophical books and thoughts, and prayed to God the Lord with fervent sighs day and night that He might graciously reveal the truth of this Art to me. Then, in my ignorance—God forgive me—as I believed no other way, after I had labored in vain with my Abbot for 23 years with great effort and diligently tended the fire day and night, I believed one could learn the secret of these matters from no human being, but must instead force it from the spirits; yet it is much more possible for humans than for spirits, as I, praise God, found in the end.

Therefore, on the said day, through the usual ceremonies and proper conjurations <note>original: *Conjurationes*; formal invocations used to summon spiritual entities.</note>, as is quite common in monasteries in Italy and Spain, I, as a monastic Exorcist <note>original: *Exorcista*. He appeared to me in the form of a black, elongated, wispy glow or shadow, without any form or shape of a human or beast, and gave me question and answer with a resonant, ringing voice, as previously reported. # LITTLE PREFACE
<note>original: *Præfatiuncula*. A Latin term for a short or modest introduction.</note>
## To the Favorable Reader.

Who the author of this little book might be is unnecessary for you to know. But as to why he wrote this, hear the reason. It is also not necessary that you know who I am. Yet know, truly and in the highest truth, that the author of this little book knows how to make the **PHILOSOPHER’S STONE** <note>original: *LAPIDEM PHILOSOPHORUM*</note>, has made and prepared it, and still has or possesses it. Since we both hold each other in high regard due to an intimate friendship and are well-disposed toward one another, I asked him—as a testimony of our friendship (as the title also implies)—to explain the three **PRINCIPLES** <note>original: *PRINCIPIA*. These are the "Tria Prima"—Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt—which alchemists believed were the three base components of all material things.</note>, or the three first foundational things, namely, **Mercury**, **Sulfur**, and Salt, and to provide a brief and simple report on whether the **Philosophical Stone** <note>original: *Lapis Philosophicus*</note> is to be sought in these or in others. Since he complied with my request in short order with this little treatise <note>original: *Tractätlein*</note>, I have decided to **share** <note>original: *communiciren*</note> it with others as well (even though I might be doing the author <note>original: *Auctori*</note> a poor or slight favor in this, since he is not in the least bit boastful),

# COLLOQUIUM or Dialogue between Nature, Mercury, and an Alchemist.

Once, the alchemists gathered and held a council to discuss how one might prepare the PHILOSOPHER’S STONE <note>original: *LAPIDEM PHILOSOPHORUM*</note>. They resolved among themselves that every person present should offer their opinion on the matter. This assembly took place under the open, free sky, upon a heath, and on a particularly bright day. There, many unanimously agreed that Quicksilver or Mercury was the first matter <note>original: *Materi*—the fundamental substance from which all metals grow</note>; others, however, believed it was Sulfur; while still others proposed something else entirely. Yet Mercury or Quicksilver was the primary subject of discussion, especially based on the writings of the Philosophers, since they present it as the true matter as well as the first matter of the metals. For the Philosophers cry and shout: "Our Mercury <note>original: <term>☿</term>us</note>, our Quicksilver," etc. While they were thus contending and struggling with one another with great effort (as each was eagerly awaiting the final resolution of this question), a severe storm suddenly arose with thunder, lightning, and hail, unheard-of wind and a downpour. This turbulence scattered the assembly, casting each individual into foreign lands and provinces, dividing and completely separating them, so that the final conclusion <note>original: *Conclusion und Schlußrede*</note> was at that time prevented, delayed, and left unfinished.

Nevertheless, in the time that followed, each one

One of them in particular, still mindful of the conversation they had held—namely, that the Philosopher’s Stone was to be prepared from <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: <term>☿io</term></note> or quicksilver—said these words to himself: "Even though no final resolution was reached, I will nonetheless work with <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: <term>☿io</term></note>, or quicksilver; indeed, I myself will provide the conclusion and the final resolution, and prepare this blessed stone." Therefore, he began to read the books of the philosophers and came across the book of ALANUS <note>likely Alan of Lille, a 12th-century scholar to whom various alchemical works were attributed</note>, where he treats <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: <term>☿io</term></note> or quicksilver.

# Concerning the Philosophical Stone <note>original: *von dem Lapide Philosophico*</note>

> **ALCHEMIST.** O heart! I know enough of the art to clean it in the best possible way with vinegar, saltpeter, and vitriol <note>vitriol: a historical term for sulfate minerals, often used as a powerful acid or solvent</note>.

At this point, the alchemist awoke from his sleep and considered within himself what kind of vision this had been. He also pondered what kind of **Mercury of the Philosophers** <note>original: *Mercurius Philosophorum*</note> this might be; yet he could think of no other quicksilver than the common kind. He wished, moreover, that he could have held a longer conversation with this old man. Nonetheless, he worked incessantly, now in the dung <note>original: *Koth*</note> of animals and small children, and soon thereafter—with your permission to speak of it—in his own dung. Meanwhile, he walked every day to the place where this vision and dream had appeared to him, so that he might (as he intended) speak further with this old man. Sometimes he also pretended as if he were sleeping, lying with his eyes closed and waiting for the old man. But when the man would no longer come, he blamed it on the idea that the old man would notice he was not truly sleeping; therefore, he swore and protested, saying:
> My dear old master, do not be afraid; truly I am sleeping; look at my eyes, if you do not want to trust me.

And this miserable alchemist, after squandering much wealth and enduring manifold toil and labor, had by now become half a fool and was almost out of his mind, as he constantly imagined this old man before him.

**ALCHEMIST.** At this, the Alchemist spoke with a joyful heart: "Now I have truly found what I sought!" and said once more with a terrible voice to Mercury: "Now then! Henceforth be obedient and subservient to me, otherwise it shall go ill with you."

**MERCURY.** "Quite gladly, my Lord, if it were only possible for me; for truly, I am currently very weak."

**ALCHEMIST.** "What? Do you still seek to make excuses?"

**MERCURY.** "No, my Lord; rather, I am completely powerless and faint."

**ALCHEMIST.** "What, then, is your grievance? Or what is harmful to you?"

**MERCURY.** "The Alchemist is superior to me and is harmful."

**ALCHEMIST.** "What, are you merely mocking me?"

**MERCURY.** "Ah, dear Lord, no! God forbid! I speak only of the Alchemist; you, however, are a Philosopher."

**ALCHEMIST.** "O, well spoken, well spoken! I am indeed. But what harm has the Alchemist done to you?"

**MERCURY.** "O my Lord, he has inflicted great evils upon me, for he has mixed me, poor soul, with many contrary things, which is why I cannot regain my strength and am half dead, for he has martyred me even unto death."

**ALCHEMIST.** Oh, it serves you right, for you are disobedient.

**MERCURY.** I have never been disobedient to any true Philosopher; rather, by the very necessity of my nature, I laugh at and mock the ignorant fools.

**ALCHEMIST.** What, then, do you think of me?

**MERCURY.** Oh, my dear sir, you are a most excellent man, a great and enlightened Philosopher; in your majesty, you surpass even Hermes <note>original: *Hermetem*, referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary father of alchemy.</note>.

**ALCHEMIST.** Yes, well said! I am indeed a learned man, though I do not wish to boast. My own wife often tells me that I am quite a skilled Philosopher—the woman has seen that much in me, at least.

**MERCURY.** I believe it indeed; for that is how one must treat "Philosophers" who turn themselves into fools through their own vanity and wit.

**ALCHEMIST.** Well then, tell me: what shall I do with you? How must I prepare the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapidem Philoſophorum*</note> from your substance?

**MERCURY.** Oh, my dear Philosopher, I do not know! You are the Philosopher, and I am but the servant of Philosophers. They are free to make of me what they will; I offer them obedience as far as I am able.

**ALCHEMIST.** You must tell me how I am to handle you, and whether I might prepare the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapidem Philoſophorum*</note> from you.

**MERCURY.** If you know the way, you shall succeed; if you do not, you shall fail. You will learn nothing from me if you do not already know it, my dear Philosopher.

**ALCHEMIST.** What? Do you speak to me as if I were some common person? Do you not know that I have <term>labored</term> <note>original: *laborirt*, referring to chemical experimentation</note> for great princes and lords, and was esteemed by them as a clever Philosopher?

**MERCURY.** I believe you well, my dear; and that is exactly why I speak as I do—for I still stink from the filth with which you besmeared me during your "beautiful" <term>labors</term>.

### Concerning the Philosopher's Stone <note>original: *von dem Lapide Philosophico*</note>

**The Riddle.** <note>original: *Aufsatz* — literally "composition" or "essay," here serving as a paradoxical description or riddle of the Stone</note> It is life, and yet it kills everything. It is a king, yet another possesses his kingdom. It flies away together with the **fire** <term>△</term> <note>the upward-pointing triangle is the alchemical symbol for the element of Fire</note>, and yet a fire is prepared from it. It is a **water** <term>∇</term> <note>the downward-pointing triangle is the alchemical symbol for the element of Water</note>, and yet it does not gnaw <note>or "corrode"; a reference to the "mercurial water" which was said to dissolve metals without being corrosive like common acids</note>. It is an earth, and yet it is sown. It is an air, and yet it lives in the water.

**ALCHEMIST.** Now I see that I know nothing; but I dare not say it, for I would lose my reputation and praise, and not one of my friends would hold me in any regard anymore. Still, I will speak and act as if I knew much; otherwise, no one would give me even a piece of bread, for there are many who hope for great wealth from me.

**NATURE.** But what if you carry on this way for a long time? What end will it take? In the end, every one of your friends will want to have back what is theirs.

**ALCHEMIST.** I will feed them all with good hope as long as I can.

**NATURE.** But what will eventually come of it?

**ALCHEMIST.** I will secretly devise many strange practices <note>original: *Practicken* — often implying fraudulent or deceptive methods</note> through laboratory work <note>original: *Laboriren*</note>; if I succeed, I will pay them. But if not, I will move to another land and keep house there in the same way.

**NATURE.** My, but what will finally come of it and follow?

**ALCHEMIST.** Ha ha, he! The world is the world, and there are many lands, and also many money-greedy people; to them I will promise great wealth, to be delivered in a short time. Thus one day passes into the next. In the meantime, Cunz or Heinz <note>idiomatic names for "one man or another," similar to "Tom, Dick, or Harry"</note>, bishop or barber <note>original: *Bader* — a bath-keeper who also performed minor surgeries</note>, king or ass will remain on the field—or I will.

**NATURE.** A rope will follow; that belongs to such "philosophers" by right. Begone, and soon put an end to yourself and your "philosophy" at the gallows. For with this single counsel, you will deceive neither me nor anyone else, much less yourself, etc.

# LULL ON THE PREPARATION OF THE
## BLESSED PHILOSOPHICAL STONE.

When we look back upon the Wise Men of former times, the minds of them all were set upon recognizing and bringing forth the hidden things of Nature, and enlightening the darkened human understanding through wisdom; for man surpasses other animals in no respect more than when, through his enlightened understanding, he wisely contemplates Nature as it is enclosed within the circles of the heavens, and brings forth natural works in accordance with such wise contemplation. ->On the preparation of the Philosopher's Stone.<-

...labored, so that their descendants might be fed with the wisdom and understanding of Nature, and not remain stuck in ignorance and the darkness of the mind, through which they deviate from human perfection and step toward the irrational beasts of a strange, wild nature. For this reason, so many various books by many learned and wise people are available, in which each one, according to his ability and pleasure, has explained and revealed his grasped or otherwise learned wisdom, and shown us by what means, manner, and way we too might obtain such established wisdom: so that we do not perhaps miss the right goal or wisdom, and be led into many kinds of wrong paths.

And although the philosophers used many different ways of speaking about one thing—so much so that one might think there is no consensus <note>original: *consensum*</note> in their writings, and therefore nothing fundamental to be found—yet one must take good heed and know that there is only one Nature spread through all creatures of the world. She maintains each kind in its own place and its own species, and lets nothing happen by chance, but rather everything stands and exists in number, weight, and measure <note>original: *numero, pondere & mensura*; a reference to the biblical Book of Wisdom 11:20, signifying that the universe is governed by mathematical and divine order.</note>. She does not depend on this or that writing, but exists for herself without writing, revealed enough to those who seek to investigate her not only with skillful, high thoughts, but also with intelligent, diligent, and clever works. ### Treatise of Raymond Lull

...to look out for, so that he does not perhaps let Nature go and devote himself alone to the books of the philosophers, from which he will then draw many different <term>opinions</term> <note>original: *opiniones*</note> that will be difficult for him to separate from one another and to pick out the right and true from the bad and wrong. Thus, Nature must be taken in hand alongside reading, and reading alongside Nature; reading must be judged by Nature, and not Nature judged by reading. This is true even though the difficult writings of the highly learned philosophers lead one a good way toward the knowledge of Nature and are, as it were, a <term>guidance</term> <note>original: *Manuductio*; literally, a "leading by the hand" or an introductory manual</note>. 

For in the consideration of Nature, after the philosophers first viewed the Heavens and their constellations, together with their constant motion, and then the four <term>elements</term> <note>original: *Elementa*; refers to Earth, Air, Fire, and Water</note> and what is contained within them, they found that the Heavens have an effect upon the elements, just as one element has an effect upon the other. It is as if the Heavens command the elements as a father commands his son and rules over them. Therefore, they considered and wrote that the Heavens are necessary <term>for generation</term> <note>original: *ad Generationem*; the process of bringing new life or matter into being</note>. Hence the common philosophical proverb states: *The Sun and man generate man.* <note>original: *Sol & Homo generant hominem*; a medieval axiom derived from Aristotle, suggesting that human life requires both biological parents and the life-giving energy of the sun.</note> 

Indeed, based on the workings of Nature, they also finely divided their writings into <term>celestial</term>, <term>animal</term>, <term>vegetable</term>, and <term>mineral</term> <note>original: *Cæleſtia, Animalia, Vegetabilia & Mineralia*</note>, because they believed that under these four categories almost all things subject to Nature were comprised. They also assigned to each thing its effect and portion according to its kind and property, and held each in the high status in which it was placed by God. Regarding the Heavens, they paid special attention to the great light...

<summary>This page argues that students of alchemy and philosophy must balance their reading with the observation of Nature to avoid being misled by conflicting opinions. It describes the hierarchical relationship between the Heavens and the four elements as the foundation for "generation" and the classification of all natural things.</summary>

# Raymond Lull’s Treatise

# Raymond Lull’s Treatise

The <term>Vital Spirits</term><note>original Latin: *Spirituum Vitalium*; the life-sustaining forces believed to circulate through the body.</note> lie within the <term>Sun</term><note>The symbol ☉ (the Sun) is the standard alchemical shorthand for gold.</note>; the more penetrating the Sun becomes, the more extensively and powerfully its strength will manifest itself. Therefore, physicians have for many years been in the habit of quenching the Sun while it is glowing hot several times in an appropriate <term>water</term><note>The symbol ∇ is the alchemical sign for water.</note>, and then giving the aforementioned water to the sick person to drink. They have also quenched the Sun in <term>waters of life</term><note>original Latin: *Aquis vitæ*; typically referring to distilled alcohol or brandy used as a solvent.</note> so that these spirits, having drawn a power from the Sun into themselves, would be all the more effective.

But other highly learned <term>philosophers</term><note>In this context, "philosophers" refers to alchemists or natural scientists.</note> were not satisfied with this. Because they saw that the Sun lost nothing in weight nor in its degree of <term>tincture</term><note>The "tincture" refers to the deep yellow color of the gold, which alchemists believed held its medicinal soul.</note> through such quenching, they concluded that no power could have departed from it, since any loss of the Sun's power would result in a decrease in its weight and color. If the tincture remains at its same degree of <term>Hungarian</term><note>Hungarian gold was famous for its high purity; the author uses "Hungarian" as a synonym for "fine" or "pure."</note> quality after the aforementioned quenching, then it remains Hungarian; if it was fine before, it remains fine afterward. Since the weight is also no less after the quenching than it was before, it follows that no power can be extracted from the Sun in such a manner.

Therefore, they sought a certain way by which the essential power could be extracted from the <term>solar corpse</term><note>The "corpse" (*corpus*) is the physical, metallic body of the gold left behind once its spiritual essence is removed.</note> and separated from it. For this reason, many different ways to make <term>Drinkable Gold</term><note>original Latin: *Aurum Potabile*; a legendary medicinal oil or liquid made from gold, believed to be a universal cure.</note> have been taught by the philosophers, such as in the works of **Hieronymus von Braunschweig**, likewise in the *Heaven of the Philosophers* by **Ulstadius**, and similarly in the book of **Antonius Famavellus** *On the Composition of Medicines*, chapter 7. Also in the writings of **Raymond Lull**, **Arnald of Villanova**, **Theophrastus Paracelsus**, and many others.

### On the Preparation of the Philosopher's Stone
<note>original Latin: de præparatione Lapidis Philosoph.</note>

It is beyond doubt that, according to the order of Nature, everything can give birth to nothing other than that which was implanted in it to produce its own seed. Likewise, whatever is implanted in any seed to be produced, that is what it brings forth and gives birth to—provided that it is a true seed in its own nature, and not perhaps corrupted or imperfect within itself, or hindered by other things. 

This can be seen in a grain of wheat: if it is not worm-eaten, and it is cast into a fertile and well-prepared soil and dies therein <note>a reference to the biblical and alchemical idea that a seed must "die" or putrefy to be reborn</note>, it brings forth wheat. The vine brings forth grapes; the olive tree, olives; and a human also gives birth to another human. This happens for no other reason than **because the species of things are distinguished by specific differences, and are preserved in their being through the succession of subsequent individuals.** <note>original Latin: "quia Species Rerum per differentias specificas sunt distinctæ, ac per successionem subeuntium individuorum in suo Esse conservantur." This is a standard scholastic argument: things stay what they are because they reproduce their own kind.</note>

Since this is the case, no <term>Vegetable</term> <note>the kingdom of plants</note> will give birth to an <term>Animal</term> <note>the kingdom of sentient creatures</note>, nor will any animal give birth to a <term>Mineral</term> <note>the kingdom of metals and stones</note>. Instead, each will give birth **within its own kind** <note>original Latin: "in suo genere"</note> to that which was implanted in its seed to be produced: the vegetable produces something vegetable, the animal something animal, and the mineral something mineral. 

As an example: no human will give birth to a herb, or a tree, or a metal. Likewise, no tree or herb will give birth to a human or a metal. Thus also, no metal will give birth to a human or a tree; rather, each will be preserved in its own species and bring forth fruit therein. Just as metal produces metal, a human produces a human, and herbs produce herbs, and so forth. **For species differing in genus can never be confused or mixed; rather, they differ from one another under their own genus by a generic difference, by which those of the same genus...** <note>original Latin: "Nam genere differentes Species nunquam confundi possunt aut queunt, sed sub suo genere à se mutuo differunt magis differentia Generica, qua ejusdem generis"</note>

<sig>L</sig>
<meta>catchword: Species</meta>

<summary>This page argues for the biological and metaphysical law of "like produces like," asserting that the three kingdoms of nature (vegetable, animal, and mineral) cannot cross-breed or produce one another. This provides the theoretical basis for the alchemical requirement that the Philosopher's Stone must be sought within the mineral/metallic kingdom.</summary>

### On the Preparation of the Philosopher’s Stone

...un-doubtable <note>The catchword from the previous page completes this as "unzweifelhaftig" or "indubitable"</note> that according to the order of **Nature**, every single thing can give birth to nothing else than that which its **seed** is planted to produce. Likewise, whatever is planted in each individual **seed** to be born, that it brings forth and gives birth to, provided it is a true **seed** in its nature and not perhaps corrupted or imperfect within itself, or hindered by other things. This can be seen in a **grain of wheat**, which, if it is not worm-eaten, when it is cast into a fertile and prepared soil and dies therein, brings forth **wheat**. The **vine** brings forth grapes, the **olive tree** olives, and **man** also gives birth to another human. This happens for no other reason than *because the species of things are distinguished by specific differences, and are preserved in their being through the succession of subsequent individuals* <note>original Latin: *quia Species Rerum per differentias specificas sunt distinctæ, ac per successionem subeuntium individuorum in suo Esse conservantur*</note>.

Since this is the case, then no **Vegetable** <note>referring to the plant kingdom</note> will give birth to an **Animal**, nor any **Animal** to a **Mineral**. Instead, every single thing will give birth *within its own kind* <note>original Latin: *in suo genere*</note> to that which its **seed** is planted to produce: the **Vegetable** produces vegetable, the **Animal** animal, and the **Mineral** mineral. For example: no human will give birth to a herb, or a tree, or a metal. Likewise, no tree or herb will give birth to a human or a metal. Thus also, no metal will give birth to a human or a tree, but each will be preserved in its own lineage <note>original: *Geschlecht*</note> and bring forth fruit therein, as metal births metal, man births man, herbs birth herbs, and so forth. *For species differing in genus can never, and are unable to, be confused, but under their own genus they differ from one another more by generic difference than those of the same genus* <note>original Latin: *Nam genere differentes Species nunquam confundi possunt aut queunt , sed sub suo genere à se mutuo differunt magis differentia Generica , qua ejusdem generis*</note>.

### Raymond Lully’s Treatise

Species differ from one another by their own constitutive difference <note>original Latin: "Species inter se differunt sua differentia seipsam constitutiva"</note>.

An example: there is a greater difference between **Vegetables** <note>meaning the plant kingdom</note> and **Animals** than there is between a **cedar tree** and **hyssop**. Likewise, there is a greater difference between **metals** and **animals** than between a **human** and an **ape**. The reason for this is because man and ape are both **animals**, and therefore they coincide *in one Genus* <note>original Latin: "in uno Genere"; a genus is a broad category containing various species</note>, even though they are understood to be *under different species* <note>original Latin: "sub diversis speciebus"</note>. For instance, a man—namely Peter—falls *under the species of man* <note>original Latin: "sub specie hominis"</note>, while this **Ape** falls *under the species of Ape* <note>original Latin: "haec Simia sub specie Simiæ"</note>. However, man and metals are not only distinguished from one another *by Species* <note>original Latin: "Specie"</note>, but also *by Genus* <note>original Latin: "Genere"</note>. The same can be said of **animals** and **plants** <note>original Latin: "Plantis"</note>; they are very far apart from one another, and for that reason they cannot give birth to each other.

Since, then, only a single **Universal Medicine** <note>original: "Universalis Medicina"; the alchemical Philosopher's Stone</note>—which was mentioned above—can cleanse both man and metals of their respective impurities, it is necessary that such a **Medicine** be taken and prepared from a suitable **Matter** <note>original: "Materia"</note>. This matter must be created by **God** in such a way that it can be brought to such a state of perfection. For indeed, whatever is to purify both man and metal must possess such power that it can drive out the impurities from both and bring them both into their state of perfection. Thus, since such cleanliness and perfection must be introduced from the outside into a human and into an imperfect metal, it is necessary that this medicine, through which this is to be performed, must first be entirely clean and perfect within itself. Furthermore, since these three are vegetable in the *vegetables* <note>original: *Vegetabilibus*; referring to the plant kingdom.</note> and animal in the *animals* <note>original: *Animalibus*</note>, it follows that they are metallic in the metallic things, and within every *species* of metals they are according to that same *species*. Otherwise, a *confusion of species* <note>original: *Confusio Specierum*</note> would arise, which is avoided through the implanted *principles* <note>original: *Principia*</note> according to each specific *species*. Therefore, the three aforementioned *principles* in gold (☉) are gold-like—acting as a gold-like Mercury (☿), a gold-like *sulfur*, and a gold-like salt. In silver <note>original: *Luna*</note>, they are silver-like; in lead <note>original: *Saturn* (♄)</note>, they are leaden; and so forth. And how could this be otherwise, since it was ordained by God the Almighty at the creation of the world when He separated the elements and commanded each element to bring forth fruit according to its innate nature, also separating all *species* from one another and giving each *species* its own kind?

# Raymond Lully’s Treatise

So then, if gold or the parts of gold had been **common mercury**, <note>original: *Mercurius Vulgi*; this refers to ordinary quicksilver sold in shops, as opposed to the "philosophical" mercury alchemists sought to extract from metals.</note> it would have to follow that common mercury is also of a **gold-like nature**, or else that there is something in gold that is not of a gold-like nature. # Tractate of Raymond Lull

Begin here—as far as it is permitted to reveal to man—and it is this: First, you shall take fine gold, purified to the highest degree through <term>quartation</term> <note>A refining process where gold is alloyed with three parts silver and then separated using acid.</note> or **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, and dissolve it in its own **Water** <note>original symbol: 🜄; likely refers to a specialized alchemical solvent like *Aqua Regia*.</note>. Then, after the <term>phlegm</term> <note>In alchemy, the "phlegm" is the tasteless, watery distillate that carries no medicinal virtue.</note> has been drawn off until the oiliness is reached, the solution, together with the oiliness, shall be placed in a cool and moist place until the dissolved gold "shoots" into crystals. After these crystals appear, they shall be transformed into a **living Mercury** through the proper means of <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The process of breaking down a substance through gentle heat, often associated with a blackening of the material.</note> and **calcination** <note>original: 🜂tion. The symbol 🜂 represents fire; calcination is the reduction of a substance to a powder through high heat.</note>. This is then the *nearest matter of the Philosopher’s Stone* <note>original: *proxima materia Lapidis Philosophorum*</note>, used to <term>tincture</term> <note>To "tincture" means to transform or imbue a substance (or a person) with a new quality or health.</note> both man and metals.

And although there is now one way to complete the entire work—in that the **Medicine** is perfectly prepared to tincture metals as well as man and to cleanse them of all impurity—yet, because this way is somewhat difficult and hidden due to the obscurity of the **Philosophical** writings, and also because of the secret maneuvers required in the **Entrance** and **Multiplication**, the **Philosophers** have sought and found a "nearer way" to preserve and restore man’s health. It is this:

After they obtained the Mercury of the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉; refers to the Mercury derived from Gold.</note>, they prepared it by itself in a suitable small glass, **precipitated** it until it became brownish-red, and then used it with great benefit for the sick. It was used effectively in cases of <term>dropsy</term> <note>Edema or swelling caused by excess fluid.</note>, the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>Epilepsy.</note>, <term>leprosy</term> <note>original: Aussatz</note>, in **gout** <note>original: *Gutta*</note> and all its various forms, in the expelling of poison, and in all violent diseases, by whatever name they might be called. ### On the Preparation of the Philosopher's Stone. <note>original Latin: *de præparatione Lapidis Philosophici*</note>

The aim of this entire art <note>original Latin: *totius ejus artis Scopus*</note> is that you may skillfully prepare the Mercury of the Sun <note>original Latin: *Mercurium scilicet Solis*; a specialized alchemical substance believed to be the "soul" or essence of gold</note>, and also recognize that even if this Mercury is not entirely sufficient for "tinging" <note>the alchemical process of dyeing or transforming base metals into gold</note> metals, it nevertheless possesses such power over the body that it is able to restore it to health.

Nevertheless, it performs its work more subtly, powerfully, and pleasantly than any other medicine. It gives the heart such strength that no pestilence <note>the plague</note> or poison can harm one's life. The sphere moves, so that it is not inconvenient to understand materially how the verse from Genesis can be applied here: *The Spirit of the Lord moved upon the waters.* <note>original Latin: *Spiritus Domini ferebatur super aquas*</note> Into such a water, the <term>Mercury of the Sun</term> <note>original symbol: ☉; representing the "solar" or purified gold-principle</note> must be resolved and transformed without the addition of any foreign thing, as the **Assembly** <note>referring to the *Turba Philosophorum*</note> says: It dissolves itself, it kills itself, and makes itself alive through *putrefaction* <note>the stage of decay and blackening</note>, which is a *grinding not of hands, but of cooking* <note>original Latin: *contritio non manuum, sed decoctionis*; meaning the matter is broken down by heat rather than physical force</note>, without which action nothing can be accomplished. *Because nothing ever becomes growing, or born, or animated, except after putrefaction; and if it has not been putrefied, it cannot be dissolved, and if it is not dissolved, it will procreate nothing.* <note>original Latin: *Quia nunquam fit aliquid concrescens vel natum vel animatum, nisi post putrefactionem, & si putridum non fuerit, non poterit solvi, & si solutum non fuerit, nihil procreabit.*</note>

Therefore, *putrefaction* is the most important thing in this work, so that through it the elements are separated, and each one is transformed into the other, and yet ultimately they must stand together under one form of *perfection*. Each element governs and accomplishes its effect in its own time, so that finally a more noble thing may be generated. In this work, **Body, Spirit, and Soul** <note>abbreviated as C. SP. & A. for *Corpus, Spiritus, & Anima*</note> are also separated, all three of which are found therein, as the **Philosophers** say: *Our Stone is composed of body, soul, and spirit,* <note>original Latin: *Lapis noster est ex corpore, Anima & Spiritu*</note> so that they may be reunited again more clearly and more perfectly.

Because of this, the Mercury appears first; then the water comes out of the Mercury by means of a dew, which rises from the earth into the air and is held within the roundness of the sphere; it also descends again as a dew into the lowest part, as **Hermes** <note>referring to Hermes Trismegistus</note> says: *The wind carried it, because the generation of our offspring takes place in the air, and being born in the air, it is born wisely.* <note>original Latin: *Portavit illum ventus, quia generatio geniti nostri fit in aëre, & nascens in aëre sapienter nascitur.*</note> Likewise elsewhere: *It ascends from the earth to the sky, and again descends to...* <note>original Latin: *Ascendit à terra in Cælum, iterumque descendit in...* This is a famous quote from the Emerald Tablet describing the circulation of the matter.</note>

...acquiring for the earth the power of the things above and the things below. <note>original Latin: *terram acquirendo vim superiorum & inferiorũ*; this is a famous reference to the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus, suggesting the material captures celestial influences.</note> All of this must then occur through the previously mentioned <term>Putrefaction of Dung</term>. <note>original Latin: *putrefactionem fimi*; a traditional alchemical technique of using the gentle, steady heat produced by fermenting horse manure to warm a vessel.</note> When, therefore, the <term>Mercury of the Sun</term> <note>original: *Mercurius ☉is*; the "solar" mercury or the purified essence of gold</note> is held in its constant warmth and long-duration cooking, and is transformed into a water through the constant motion it performs in its sphere, it begins—on account of the constant rising and descending—to become ever a little thicker and browner. 

And in the event that something corporeal [material] should still show itself, which had not yet been perfectly transformed into the vaporous water, it would nevertheless be converted into a spiritual body through the complete and perfect rising and falling and circular motion in the sphere, and also brought into water. Thus, all parts of the Mercury of the Sun are of one nature, and each can be brought to where the other is, even though one happens more slowly than the other; yet this is not because they are of unequal nature, but because the parts of the Mercury are not all raised at once. Rather, one after another passes through the sphere, and that which has passed through the sphere most often is always the first to be resolved into water. 

When finally all parts of the Mercury of the Sun have sufficiently passed through their sphere, they are ultimately all resolved into one water, which, as mentioned, becomes thicker and browner through the same cooking. Therefore, the water is not to be changed, nor the vessel, even if the <term>Solution</term> <note>the process of a solid turning into a liquid state</note> of the Mercury does not manifest all at once; for it can well be accomplished in one governance of the fire and in one vessel, even if it happens successively. Therefore, the entire art is nothing other than <term>Solution and Coagulation</term>. <note>original Latin: *Solutio & Coagulatio*; the fundamental alchemical maxim describing the cycle of dissolving a substance and then solidifying it again to purify it.</note>

# On the preparation of the Philosopher's Stone.

...of the Philosopher's Stone in proper <term>Putrefaction</term>. <note>The stage of "putrefaction" in alchemy represents a symbolic death and decomposition of the base material, usually indicated by the substance turning black.</note> Therefore the Philosophers say that the practitioner of our work must first dissolve the Stone, then coagulate it, since our work is nothing other than making a perfect solution and coagulation. <note>original Latin: *quòd artifex nostri operis primò debeat Lapidem solvere, deinde coagulare, cum opus nostrum nihil aliud sit, quam facere perfectam solutionem & coagulationem.* This refers to the famous alchemical maxim "Solve et Coagula."</note> And further: Unless everything is turned into Water, one can in no way arrive at the art; for these two—namely the Solution of the body and the Coagulation of the Spirit— <margin>|</margin> emerge in one single operation, and one does not happen without the other. <note>original Latin: *Nisi quodlibet vertatur in Aquam, nullatenus pervenitur ad artem; Hæc enim ambo, scilicet Solutio corporis & Coagulatio Spiritus exeunt in operatione una, & non fit unum sine altero.*</note> For to dissolve the body is to coagulate the Spirit, which is the Work of Nature. However, it is not advisable to do this, because the glass is not to be opened before the end of the work, and the oil becomes more and more perfect the longer it remains sealed in its <term>Putrefaction</term>. Then, after the spirit, the soul shall be brought forth; this is the true *Fixed Incombustible Oil of Gold*, which penetrates, exalts, and makes perfect all metals.

### On the preparation of the Philosopher's Stone

When, therefore, first the Mercury of the Sun has transformed itself through proper <term>putrefaction <note>the alchemical stage of decay or fermentation, often symbolized by the color black, where the substance breaks down to be reborn</note></term> into water, and then that water has changed into a lemon-brown oil, then two Natural Principles have perfectly appeared: Mercury in the form of <term>Water <note>original symbol: ∇; representing the philosophical element of Water or the volatile spirit</note></term>, and Sulfur in the form of a lemon-brown oil. And since this oil makes the metals into gold, that which was previously hidden has been brought forth once again, which before was concealed. 

And thus, the fulfillment of the Philosophical Rule has occurred here: <note>original Latin: "ut occultum manifestetur, & manifestum occultetur"</note> *that what is hidden may be made manifest, and what is manifest may be hidden.* For what is more hidden in <term>Gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note></term> than its golden mercury? For while gold withstands <term>Fire <note>original symbol: Δ</note></term>, its mercury flees from it; therefore, it seems impossible that gold should be transformed into a mercury, and that which is fixed should become volatile. What, in turn, is more hidden in the Golden Mercury than this lemon-brown oil, which transforms metals into <term>Gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note></term>? It not only returns to its own first nature of its own accord but also brings other metals into that same nature. 

Therefore the Philosophers say: <note>original Latin: "Exteriora Auri, sunt interiora Argenti, scilicet vivi, & interiora auri, sunt exteriora Argenti, scilicet vivi."</note> *The outward parts of Gold are the inward parts of Silver—that is, of quicksilver—and the inward parts of Gold are the outward parts of Silver—that is, of quicksilver.* For within gold, the whiteness of mercury lies hidden and does not appear; likewise, within mercury, the redness of gold lies hidden and does not appear, unless the <term>Spagyrist <note>a practitioner of alchemical medicine and separation, from the Greek words for "to tear apart" and "to bind together"</note></term> through his wisdom brings such redness forth again. 

Gold appears as gold through and through; all its parts are red. Nevertheless, it is transformed into the <term>Whitish Eagle <note>a traditional alchemical term for a volatile, purified white substance, usually a mercurial salt or sublimate</note></term>, so that it loses its redness. So too, the whitish eagle or Mercury of the Sun appears white through and through, yet nonetheless the highest redness of gold remains hidden beneath it,

# On the preparation of the Philosophers' Stone.

It is also not necessary that one enter into a special path here, *because the white and red proceed from one root, as Arnold <note>original: "Quia album & Rubeum ex una procedunt radice, Arnoldo teste"; referring to Arnold of Villanova (c. 1240–1311), a famous physician and alchemist.</note> testifies:* Rather, it requires only a longer time and constant cooking. With the fire one cannot err after the whiteness, *because in this whiteness the **REDNESS** is hidden,* <note>original: "post albedinem, quia in hac albedine RUBOR est occultus"</note> which redness must then be brought forth solely through longer cooking.

*Therefore, let it be cooked with a dry fire (as the Turba of the Philosophers <note>The "Turba Philosophorum" is one of the oldest Latin alchemical texts, presented as an assembly of ancient philosophers.</note> says) and dry calcination, until it turns red as Cinnabar; to which decoction you should by no means add water, nor any other thing, until the Red is cooked to completion; it will give the eternal color of Gold.* <note>original: "Igne igitur sicco (ut ait Turba Philosophor.) & calcinatione sicca decoquatur, donec rubeat ut Cinabrium, cui decoctioni nequaquam imponas aquam, neque aliam rem, quousque ad complementum coquatur Rubeum, dabit colorem Auri perpetuum."</note> Therefore, there are some old verses:

> So that the **ROSE** might not just grow white, but shine with light,
> Just let it boil constantly, and rest in its heat,
> Until it gives forth splendor and brings out brilliance;
> The white generates Whiteness, the red generates Redness.
> <note>original Latin: "Ut non candescat ROSA, verùm luce lucescat, / Tantùm fervescat jugiter, fervore quiescat, / Donec splendorem tribuat, tollatque nitorem ; / Candida Candorem generat, Rubicunda Ruborem."</note>

Therefore, one should proceed further with the constant <term>△</term><gloss>Fire</gloss> of the philosophers, until the whiteness has passed, and after several lemon-yellow colors, a redness follows like a high scarlet, which is then the highest Tincture. And even if such colors appear, one should still let it stand for another month or two and not open the glass; in this way, it becomes even more beautiful, and indeed, one becomes all the more certain of the <term>fixation</term> <note>Fixation is the process of making a substance volatile (likely to evaporate) into a "fixed" state where it can endure the fire without being consumed.</note>. But when one now believes that it is entirely ready, one should take the Medicine out and let a little of it flow onto a glowing <term>☽</term><gloss>Silver</gloss> plate. If it flows without smoke like wax, then the Medicine is perfect and the Tincture is ready—to cleanse, to strengthen, to improve, and to make perfect both human beings and metals. But if it smokes, it must be put back inside and stand even longer until it is fixed enough. When all this is finally accomplished, then this

### Raymund Lull’s Treatise

The Medicine of Kings, of which the Philosophers say: *That here is born a King crowned with a Triple Diadem, shining like the Sun, glowing more brightly than a Carbuncle, flowing like wax, enduring and retaining living mercury, and converting it into a tawny Lion.* <note>original Latin: "Quod hic generatus sit Rex Triplici Diademate coronatus, fulgens ut Sol, lucens clarius Carbunculo, fluens ut cera, perseverans & retinens ☿um vivum, ipsumque in fulvum Leonem convertens." The "Carbuncle" refers to a deep red gemstone, and the "tawny Lion" is a traditional alchemical symbol for the final, potent red stage of the Stone.</note>

Now, when one wishes to use this high Medicine for tinting <note>the process of transmuting base metals into gold</note>, the most important part after the work is finished is the **Entry** <note>original: "Ingressus," the stage where the medicine is made capable of penetrating and merging with a metal</note>. Although many Philosophers have known the right art of preparing the Philosophers’ Stone, few among them have understood the **Entry**, and therefore they did not reach a fruitful end. To prevent such misfortune, this is the means to successfully complete, understand, and note the **Entry**, which must be kept secret. Namely, that one takes one part of the red prepared Medicine, as mentioned, for every hundred parts of Gold (O) Calx <note>a fine powder produced by heating metal until it oxidizes or crumbles</note>, which is known to the <term>Spagyrist</term> <note>a practitioner of spagyric alchemy, which focuses on the separation and recombination of natural substances</note>. Grind these diligently together on a smooth, fine grinding stone, or <term>Porphyry</term> <note>a hard, purple-red stone slab used by alchemists to grind materials into the finest possible powder</note>. Then put all of this together into a well-sealed crucible, as is appropriate, and place it in a furnace that is suitable for the purpose and not too large. Give it Fire (△) gradually until everything becomes unified. Once this has happened, it is prepared for tinting.

And it should be well noted here that the right time must not be overlooked, as is known to the Philosopher, and thus this means of preparing the **Entry** should be handled with diligence. For although the Medicine is brought to its power and full perfection, it still will not enter into any metal—neither the perfect nor imperfect bodies—without this mentioned means. ### On the Preparation of the Philosophers' Stone

Even if one were to melt them for a hundred years, they would not merge without the aforementioned means, because due to their great and high purity, they would only swim on top of the melted or flowing metals, like an <term>Oil</term> <note>original Latin: Oleum</note> upon <term>Water</term> <note>original Latin: Aqua</note>. Therefore, the **Entry** must be well observed; when it is properly known and the process is correctly followed, this **Philosophers' Stone** becomes brittle like glass and inflexible. 

When all this has occurred—the union of the Medicine with the <term>Calx of the Sun</term> <note>original Latin: Calce Solis; "Calx" refers to a metal reduced to a fine powder through heat, and "the Sun" is the alchemical name for Gold</note> is ready and everything is correctly accomplished—then 1 part of this prepared Medicine should be taken, which one should cast upon 1000 parts of other imperfect metals; thus, from the mentioned metals, good, lasting gold will result in all tests. 

In the event, however, that such gold is still brittle, one should add more of the metal intended for <term>tinting</term> <note>original: tingiren; the process of transmuting or "dyeing" base metals into gold or silver</note> until the <term>Tincture</term> is properly united with the metals and the correct malleability is achieved. Therefore, when the cast-in Medicine has flowed with the metals for half an hour, one should reach into the crucible with an iron wire; whatever remains hanging on it should be hammered very thin on a clean anvil. One will then soon see if it is still inflexible.

## MULTIPLICATION IN QUALITY.

First, you should know that very few among the **Philosophers** have known the secret of **Multiplication**, primarily because of the matter of **weight**. For in the beginning of this work, no specific weight is required; but after its completion, a weight must first be employed for the sake of the <term>Ingress</term> <note>original: Ingres; the ability of the alchemical stone to "enter" or penetrate and transform a base metal or the human body</note>. This was known to few **Philosophers**, which is why this **Philosophers' Stone** <note>original Latin: Lapis Philosophorum</note> should be used upon the **Human Body** <note>original Latin: Corpus Humanum</note>, about which much could be written.
