# DEDICATORY PREFACE

->TO<-

## *The Most Illustrious Prince and Lord,*

# Lord JOACHIM ERNST,
<note>Joachim Ernst (1583–1625) was the Margrave of Brandenburg-Ansbach, a significant patron of the arts and learning during the early 17th century.</note>

->Margrave of Brandenburg, Duke of Prussia, Silesia,<-
->Stettin, Pomerania, Crossen, of the Cassubians and<-
->the Vandals, Burgrave of Nuremberg,<-
->Prince of Rügen, etc. His most<-
->clement Lord,<-

Margrave, shining with great-souled virtue and
Heroic grace, courageous Duke of your fatherland’s soil,
O Joachim Ernst, hear me, most illustrious Prince,
The serene STAR of the house of Brandenburg.
A seventh winter has flowed by, and a seventh summer turns,
While I, a wretched exile, wander far from my ancestral hearth,
Tossed by fortune's countless storms,
While I tarry as a stranger in an unknown region.
Hardly do these seven years seem to have passed for me,
Because I have borne every adversity with a patient mind.
Sacred Poetry was close to my heart at every time;
It gave me and mine our meager sustenance.
But the unclean world, while it rejects all sacred things
And denies hospitality to the sacred Muses,
Refuses us helping hands,
Alas, in ways too ungrateful, in both heart and speech.
<note>original: "Mundus at imūdus." A Latin wordplay: "Mundus" means "the world," but also "clean/neat," while "immundus" means "unclean/foul."</note>
Yet I have by no means cast away hope. JEHOVAH himself
Covers and rules me, despite my unwilling enemies.
Unless His word had sustained me and mine
In these narrow straits and miserable condition,
And given me solace even without great material harvest,
Our shipwrecked vessel would have been submerged in the waters.

# PREFACE.

Long ago, the mild ruler of spacious Olympus
&nbsp;&nbsp;Averted this evil from our Country by his goodness,
While only the Glory of Christ is sought by me,
&nbsp;&nbsp;Not my own, but the divine Glory of the heavenly Father.
By His gift, I despise any opposition—
&nbsp;&nbsp;The envious arrows and threats of a deceitful tongue.
Therefore, when my Sacred Poetry is troublesome to anyone:
&nbsp;&nbsp;What means of support might come forth for me?
My mind also persuades me to bid farewell to our Muses shortly,
&nbsp;&nbsp;Not without reason, while the heavy storm-cloud thunders.
At God’s invitation, I pass over to the Medical arts of Apollo
&nbsp;&nbsp;And to the camp of the Paracelsian school.
<note>Apollo is the classical god of healing; the "Paracelsian school" refers to the followers of Paracelsus (1493–1541), who revolutionized medicine through chemistry and mineral remedies.</note>
Namely, the study which I have cultivated for many years
&nbsp;&nbsp;By keeping watch over Hermetic books.
<note>Hermetic books: Texts attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy and "Hermetic" philosophy.</note>
Behold, it pleased me soon to visit the metal-bearing mountains,
&nbsp;&nbsp;To learn thoroughly of Nature's hidden Chaos,
<note>Chaos here refers to the "Prima Materia" or first matter, the raw, unrefined substance alchemists believed was necessary to begin the Great Work.</note>
And I ran through the tracts of Tyrol, then
&nbsp;&nbsp;Styria was seen by me and the suitability of the place;
Then, overcoming the Peaks of the Carinthian land,
&nbsp;&nbsp;I saw, by the mediation of a favorable God,
The happy seats, the thrice-blessed places, in which
&nbsp;&nbsp;Our [leader] often desired to be—
The Great Apollo of Germany, its Glory, Theophrastus,
&nbsp;&nbsp;Inspired by the heavenly star of the Holy Power.
<note>original: "Theophrastus." This refers to Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus.</note>
While traveling, I collect the many writings of the Sages,
&nbsp;&nbsp;But especially for my Country, Leader Joachim,
Concerning the great Miracle of the thrice-BLESSED STONE,
&nbsp;&nbsp;Than which no greater Good exists in the whole world.
<note>The "thrice-blessed stone" is the Philosopher’s Stone (Lapis Philosophorum), the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and granting eternal life.</note>
For the public benefit, and for the "little sons of doctrine," I judged
&nbsp;&nbsp;That it should be shared immediately as part of my duty.
From which, while this our little Hermetic Garden leaps forth 
&nbsp;&nbsp;Into the nourishing light, O Great MARGRAVE, favor it;
Under the greening shadow of your August name,
&nbsp;&nbsp;It desires the faithful protection of your patronage,

# The Little Book of **Theophrastus** with the Heavenly Bagpipes, dedicated to a Princely Person.

In G**o**d’s name I wish to tell Your Princely Grace the true secret <note>original: *Heimlichkeit*</note> of the philosophers, which the wise have kept hidden for a long time, and recounted only through parables, as the philosopher **GEBER** <note>The Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan (c. 721–815), a prolific alchemist whose works were foundational to Western alchemy.</note> speaks of.

There once went a traveler, like one who seeks something, who wandered or lost his way, and came so far that he feared he could not return; but he pressed on so far until he came into a lovely pleasure garden. Within it stood trees with many branches, which were adorned with much fruit; these then refreshed the traveler so that he partially forgot his sorrowful mind. Thus, he pressed on even further, until he came to a beautiful castle. It belonged to a king who had six daughters, who were to tend to and guard the house and the garden. And as he came to the first gate, he was met by a red man, very ugly and misshapen, who nevertheless spoke to him with mild words, asking what he was searching for there, for he had never found anyone so close to the house. He gave him his answer and said: He sought the <term>Philosopher's Stone<note>original Latin: *Lapidem Philosophorum*. The legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and providing an elixir of life.</note></term>. The red man said to him: Since you have come so far, I will guide you further; you shall go until you come to a yellow man, who will be gentle with you in all his actions, although he is ugly

# Now begins the true DRINKABLE GOLD, with words expressed / how the right art shall be made / in which no lack or fault shall be found.

Now, in the name of God, [take] your sky-blue stone, called the <term>Vitriol of the Wise <note>original: *Vitriolum Sapientum*. Not actual vitriol (sulfate), but a symbolic starting material in alchemy said to contain the "spirit" of the work.</note></term>, and well known to all the Sages; in colors black, white, green, yellow, and red; which is of a noble nature, soft to the touch, heavy in weight, sour to the taste, with a lingering sweetness. The <term>Laton <note>original: *Laton*. An alchemical term for an impure metal, often copper or brass, that must be purified until it shines like gold.</note></term> is found everywhere, not only in shops, but also among young children; those with great hearts also use it in honor or dishonor of Kings and Emperors. Of this stone take as much as you wish, and place the **Laton** in its glass to distill the sweet 🜄 <note>alchemical symbol for water</note> with gentle 🜂 <note>alchemical symbol for fire</note> until the white smoke wishes to rise; after that, let it grow cold and break the glass, and so you shall find the **delicate red man**. Thereafter, crush the material and put it into another glass. You shall keep the sweet 🜄 <note>alchemical symbol for water</note> and set the receiver before it again, as was done before, and burn the high vinegar, the <term>Virgin’s Milk <note>original: *Lac Virginis*. A white, acidic liquid used as a solvent in alchemical experiments.</note></term>, from the **yellow man** with a strong fire, just as one burns <term>Parting Water <note>original: *Scheidwasser*. Nitric acid, used to separate gold from silver.</note></term>, for 8 days and nights. Thus Your Princely Grace shall see, time and again, the white smoke of the strong **Virgin’s Milk**, or of the strong vinegar, for up to 30 days or hours; finally, a little water comes. Your Princely Grace should drive this for as long as it will flow, and Your Princely Grace should not let the labor vex you; although not much comes, it is nonetheless rich in virtue, for the last is better than the first, and both should remain kept together. For they should not come far from one another: the Heaven, which one calls the three elements; the fourth

### The Second Practice.

Furthermore, Your Princely Grace should take—in the name of the <term>Lord</term>—the high <term>vinegar</term> <note>In alchemical texts, "vinegar" often refers to a concentrated acid or a potent solvent rather than common household vinegar.</note> purified as described above, in a strong glass, and place it in the ashes <note>A "sand bath" or "ash bath" used to provide even, indirect heat.</note>, well-sealed all around so that it stands immovable and is not disturbed until the end of the work; and pay special attention to the weight. Thus, take some of the strong <term>vinegar</term> and add to it an equal weight of the sweet water <note>original: *süssen Wasser*. A purified distillate mentioned in previous steps.</note> that has been purified as stated above. Fix a <term>still-head</term> <note>original: *Helm*. The top part of a distilling apparatus.</note> upon it and <term>extract</term> <note>original: *detrahirt*. To draw off or distill away.</note> the sweet water <note>original: $\nabla$. The alchemical symbol for water.</note> from it; the <term>vinegar</term> will remain at the bottom, for it is heavy and does not rise easily. When the glass has cooled, return the distilled water back to it and draw it off again. Repeat this pouring on and drawing off so often until the <term>vinegar</term> becomes a crystal in the color of a beautiful ruby; Your Princely Grace shall see this when the glass becomes cold. Now Your Princely Grace possesses both a human and metallic <term>medicine</term> <note>Paracelsus taught that the "Stone" or "Elixir" could heal both the human body and "cure" base metals into gold.</note>, which converts all metals—after their proper justification and preparation—into <term>gold</term>, as you know; this is certain. However, should you run out of the sweet water (which is unlikely), prepare more for yourself as you did at the beginning, and give it to the <term>stone</term> which is called the <term>growing stone</term>; it is without end, and you require no <term>ferment</term> in its composition and birth.

### Concerning the Matter of the Philosophers' Stone <note>original: *Materia Lapidis Philosophorum*</note>

God is highly esteemed; therefore, this high gift is also known to few and given to few. For the sake of sin, it remains hidden. For no one attains this high gift by his own power or through much brooding <note>original: *spintisirn*. This refers to excessive, abstract speculation or intellectualizing without practical or divine insight.</note>. As far as the preparation <note>original: *Zubereitung*</note> and dissolution <note>original: *Aufflösung*</note> are concerned—to open the secret fountainhead, this secret vein and these passages from which the green and sky-colored balsam <note>In alchemy, "green" often represents the raw, living energy of nature, while "sky-colored" refers to the celestial or spiritual essence.</note> comes forth entirely spiritually and flows into our water—in that same revelation of how the **preparation** <note>original: *Praeparation*</note> occurs, all **philosophers** <note>original: *Philosophi*. Here meaning alchemists.</note> are secretive and "unfaithful" <note>The author suggests that alchemists intentionally hide the truth or give misleading instructions to prevent the unworthy from succeeding.</note>, so that it does not become common for the sake of the wicked. 

For this juice unites with the gold, and through this water the bonds of the **Sun** <note>original: *Solis*. The alchemical name for gold.</note> are opened. For thus all things which possess the color of a tincture within them are entangled by their first father, and have flowed and come forth from the first single origin out of the **Matrix** <note>original: *Matrice*. The "womb" or source of all minerals.</note> and **Sea Water** <note>original: *Aqua maris*.</note>. By God’s command, they were locked away in a chest; through this, all works are born and created for the world out of this single thing. Therein the inhabitant remains hidden; we have no use for it unless it is first opened by the salt with which it was firmly bound. These things unite: from this, our tincture or Universal Stone becomes manifest. 

But through the first Fall <note>Referring to the biblical Fall of Man in Eden.</note>, all things—which were created so pure, sheer, and clear—have again been darkened and obscured, made deadly and corruptible, and have become transitory. Therefore, all souls have needed a single Redeemer, and not many redeemers. That same Redeemer, with one tiny drop of his eternal, heavenly, fiery, rose-colored tincture, has **tinctured** <note>In alchemy, to "tinge" or "tincture" means to fundamentally transform the inner nature of a substance, just as the blood of Christ was thought to transform the soul.</note> many innumerable parts of souls, making them immortal out of death and highly glorified <note>original: *celebrificirt*</note>.

## NOTE on the Philosophers’ Stone.

The Philosophers' Stone <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note> is thus recognized and revealed through the high understanding of the Sages, left here for us. Through such food, our stone first attains the power of the perfect Tincture and its highest active virtue. This is the advice of the Sages; thus should one handle this secret: commending the soul, spirit, and the living body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of the work to God. ## Preface.

It is to be known that all things come from God,
and without Him nothing can be
made, as you find it in Genesis 1
and in the Gospel of John 1. Therefore, in
all our doings we should call upon God and
ask Him for reason and understanding for this
holy work, as all philosophers say—such as
Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of the "Hermetic" arts</note>, Arnold of Villanova <note>original: *Arnoldus de V. Nova*; a 13th-century physician and influential alchemical writer</note>, and Pallentin—
and John at the last <note>A reference to the end of the Gospel of John</note>, stating that such things must be
learned from God, not that we should want to
force our way through with our own self-
willed heads, whether God allows
Nature to permit it or not. They do
not account for that, but simply forge ahead;
one says it is hidden in wine; another in
imperfect bodies <term>base metals</term> <note>Metals like lead or tin, which alchemists believed were "impure" versions of gold</note>, in blood, in marcasite <note>A metallic mineral often confused with iron pyrites</note>,
in Mercury <note>represented by the symbol ☿</note>, in sulfur, in vitriol of copper <note>represented by the symbols □ ♀</note>, in tin <note>represented by the symbol ♃</note>, in antimony <note>represented by the symbol ⊕</note>,
in iron <note>represented by the symbol ♂</note>, in orpiment <note>original: *Auripigment*; a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, and in herbs, such as
Celandine <note>original: *Chelidonia*; a plant often associated with gold because of its yellow sap</note>, spring-root <note>A legendary plant believed to have the power to open locks or blast rocks</note>, ivy, etc. It is
all together nothing but roguery and thievery.

<meta>This page continues the preface of Caspar Hartung’s treatise. <header>Preface.</header>

...so that they deceive people and deprive them of their money; they consume and lose time wastefully and uselessly, and simply follow their own foolish heads, which cannot calculate beforehand what necessity requires. Dear friend, tell me one thing: Who must burn *aqua fortis* <note>original: *Aq. f.*, literally "strong water," refers to nitric acid, a common solvent in early chemistry</note> in the mines of the earth? Or are there people in there who distill wine or bring child’s urine <note>original: *Kinderharm*; human waste was frequently used in pre-modern chemical experiments for its ammonia content</note> so that one might make metals <term>Metalla</term>? Or do you think there are apothecaries inside the earth who have all things for sale so that you can make lead, tin, silver, gold, copper, or iron? You fool! 

Can you not understand that you are mistaken, and that none of those things belong to Nature <term>Natur</term>? Or do you want to be above GOD: that you want to make metal out of blood? If so, then make a human out of a horse, or make a cow out of a wall <note>original: *Mau-*, likely *Mauer* (wall). The author is listing biological and physical impossibilities to mock the alchemists</note>; she would then give you good milk as well—that would indeed be a multiplication <term>Multiplication</term> <note>The alchemical stage where the power or quantity of the Stone is increased</note>. 

But it does not happen; and just as little as that can happen, just as little can you make metal for me out of the aforementioned things. But if you wish to make metals <term>Metalla</term>, then pay closer attention to the philosophers <term>Philosophos</term> <note>A term for "natural philosophers" or experienced alchemists</note> and how they teach you to understand Nature <term>Natur</term>. For Art <term>Kunst</term> <note>The human skill of alchemy</note> is no more than Nature; what Nature has not created, Art can have no effect upon.

# On the Preparation of the Blessed Stone.

...stop the mouths of others, and put an end to their evil intentions, and also so that it is not said that I correct others according to my own will, but rather with good arguments. Therefore, I tell you: if this were true <note>Referring to the claim that Art can operate independently of Nature.</note>, it would not be necessary for Nature to exist at all, because Art <note>In this context, "Art" refers to the practice of alchemy or medicine.</note> would make the seed of all things, and humans from the elements alone, without Nature; and without any natural change, Art would make the beginning of the composition. This is against all reason, for Nature brings forth, and has brought forth, and only then does Art help her. It would also follow that a physician <note>original: "Medicus"</note> through his art of herbs could awaken a dead man, or that he could make a dying man healthy, which is against the words of **Avicenna** <note>Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), an influential Persian polymath and physician whose works were central to medieval European medicine.</note> and **Rhazes** <note>Al-Razi (c. 865–925), a Persian physician and alchemist who emphasized observation and experimentation.</note>, where they say the following:

> **Medicine is only a helper to Nature; for where Nature is not present, medicine can have no effect; for a laxative <note>A substance used to stimulate the bowels; here used as a metaphor for any medical treatment requiring a living biological response.</note> does not purge in a dead body,**

unless it is directed according to Nature. For thus says **Hippocrates** <note>The ancient Greek physician (c. 460 – c. 370 BC), widely considered the father of Western medicine.</note> in his Aphorisms <note>A famous collection of medical principles and observations.</note>:

> **Art acts only upon a thing created by Nature and gives it help: And Art helps this matter, and Nature helps Art.**

# Chapter VIII.

### How one should prepare the bodies when one wishes to transform them into their first matter, etc.

Take one mark <note>a historical unit of weight, usually about 8 ounces</note> of fine, pure **silver** <note>indicated by the symbol ☽</note>, filed small and rubbed clean on a stone with common salt; dissolve the salt away with hot water and let the **silver calx** <note>original: *☽ Kalck*; a fine metallic powder produced by chemical processing</note> settle to the bottom; pour the water away. Then <term>imbibe</term> <note>original: *imbibire*; to saturate or soak a solid with a liquid</note> the calx three times with **oil of tartar** <note>original: *Oleo tartari*; a concentrated solution of potassium carbonate</note>; always let the oil dry back into the silver calx. Afterward, put the calx into a glass and pour oil of tartar over it to the height of two fingers so that it is well covered; seal the glass at the top and let it stand in **horse manure** <note>original: *Roßmist*; used as a natural, steady source of gentle warmth for incubation</note> for 8 days so that it may <term>putrefy</term> <note>original: *faule*; to break down through warmth and moisture</note>; then remove the oil and dry the calx, and put it into the aforementioned living water over a gentle heat; thus the calx transforms subtly into **mercury** <note>indicated by the symbol ☿</note>; let it stand until it is completely converted into mercury. Afterward, gently pour off the water and put the **mercury of the body** <note>original: *Mercurium Corporis*; mercury extracted from a "dead" metal like silver</note> into a glass, and clean it with salt and vinegar, and dry it, and strain it through a **fine cloth** <note>original: *Parchet*; a filter, likely of fustian or parchment-like material</note>; if it passes through completely, that is good; but if any of the silver calx remains that was not entirely dissolved, put it back into the blessed water so that it may be completely transformed into mercury without any error; and this is the mercury drawn up from the **body** <note>original: *Leichnam*; the solid metal</note>, which is now called **corporeal mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius corporalis*</note>, and it is not common mercury, but rather the **mercury of the philosophers** <note>original: *Mercurius Philosophorum*</note>. Signs of this mercury are: that it is slow in its movement and not like common mercury, for it leaves its pale earth behind it in the fire.

# Chapter I.
## The Description of the Art / and Interpretation of Alchemy / what it truly is.

In many and more ancient books and writings of the philosophers, the description and interpretation of this very art is found quite openly; therefore, in this first chapter, we must take note of that same opinion and interpretation. Regarding this, Hermes the Philosopher <note>original: "Hermes der Philosophus"; refers to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many alchemical works were attributed</note> writes to us and explains it thus: Alchemy is an art of metals / or metallic things made out of one / and through one, simply composed / and also a joining together of the most noble things / which overcome one another / joined or composed through knowledge and reality / and by this same natural mixing, a genus of metals is transformed / and changed into a better state.

Another philosopher writes thus: Alchemy is an art that teaches how to transform all kinds of metals / one into the other / and this must happen through its own <term>medicine</term> <note>original: Medicinam; in alchemy, this refers to the substance (the Stone or Elixir) that "heals" base metals into gold</note> or remedy / which is then made manifest / and is written of in many books of the philosophers. And concerning this, it is to be known / that Alchemy is such an art / which is named after a philosopher who was called and named Alchymus <note>A common medieval tradition attempted to trace the name of the art back to a specific person named Alchymus</note>, and the art teaches many a medicine / that is / a remedy, which is called the <term>Elixir</term>. This same Elixir / if one throws it upon <note>original: auffwerfft; referring to the "projection" of the powder onto molten metal</note> the imperfect metal / makes the same perfect and good: That is the reason for its invention.

## Chapter II.
### On the Origin of Metals.

In the words just written, I have fulfilled and completed the first chapter: And now in the second, I will fully explain the beginning of minerals / or the ores of the mines / how and from what they naturally first sprang and were created. And regarding this, it is first to be noted / that the origin of minerals / ore or mining is nothing other / than ☿ <note>The symbol for Mercury or *Mercurius*</note> and Sulphur; from those two things all metals are created and born.

For that reason, they are of many and various forms / and are also reversed / one different from the other: But Nature always intended / and set before herself the goal to make Gold: But the contrary and various accidents / which occurred during the process / created various and contrary metals through transformation / as is then written and found quite clearly in many books of the philosophers. For according to whether the two aforementioned, Sulphur and Mercury, are pure or impure / so accordingly the metals are also created or born / such as Gold, Silver, Copper, Lead, Tin, and Iron.

Now to write of Gold: it is a perfect and pure metal, created and born from a pure and fixed <term>Sulphur</term> <note>In alchemy, "Sulphur" refers to the active, combustible, and masculine principle of "soul," not merely the chemical element</note>, which is clear and red / and has no infirmity. That [the following] is a pure metal / and almost perfect / and yet not entirely / and it is created from a pure and almost fixed <term>Mercury</term> <note>The "Mercurius" principle represents the passive, fluid, and feminine principle of "spirit"</note>, and from a clear / white and almost fixed sulfur / and it lacks a little <term>cooking</term> <note>original: "Kochung"; refers to the alchemical process of maturation or digestion through heat</note> and fixation / and thus it lacks in color / and in weight. <note>This description refers to Silver, which alchemists believed was "incomplete" gold that lacked the final "redness" and density brought by further heat in the earth.</note>

<summary>In this chapter, Poyselius explains the alchemical theory of the "Sulfur-Mercury" dyad, asserting that all metals are composed of these two principles and that base metals are simply "imperfect" or "accidental" versions of gold.</summary>

## Chapter III.

### Here follows further from what the Elixir shall be made.

IN the aforementioned and now proven writings, enough has been described and completed regarding the creation of metals, both the **perfect** <note>Gold and silver</note> and the **imperfect** <note>Base metals like lead, tin, copper, and iron</note>. So we shall now turn ourselves back to the making and accomplishing of the **Medicine of metals** <term>Medicine of metals (another term for the Philosopher's Stone or Elixir, capable of "healing" base metals into gold)</term>. 

As we have been sufficiently and clearly informed in the prescribed chapters that all metals are created and grown from **Mercury and Sulfur** <note>original: "Mercurio und Sulphure"</note>, and that it is the purity or impurity of these two that completes or ruins the metals, making them either perfect or imperfect. There is also nothing in the world that can or may be attached to the metals, or create a darkness within them, unless it is composed of these two, or has sprung from them. It is now enough to know that no outward thing is capable or sufficient to improve the metals, to perfect them, or to make any kind of transformation in them from new substances. 

Therefore, it is a wonder that a **subtle man** <note>A person who considers himself clever or sophisticated</note>—and one who thinks himself certain—would base his foundation and his opinion upon **vegetables** <term>Vegetabilia (growing things like plants, which some alchemists mistakenly believed could be used for transmutation)</term> or upon other foreign things; especially since enough **minerals** <note>original: "Mineralia"</note> (that is, ore and mined materials) are found which are close to the nature of metals.

You must not believe or think that the **Philosophers** <note>The ancient alchemical authorities</note> have placed or written of the Art in these aforementioned foreign things, except only as a **parable** <note>original: "Gleichnuß"</note>. For from the two aforementioned things, Sulfur and Mercury, arise all

Therefore, we excuse ourselves from taking them in their raw state—the **Mercury** and **Sulfur**—as they are in themselves in their own nature, since we do not know their proper composition and boiling. ### Why the Art is to be Practiced.

Therefore be praised the almighty God forever and eternally / Amen.

<summary>This page describes the practical application and "multiplication" of the alchemical Elixir, explaining how a single part can transform a million parts of metal through gradual dilution and heat. It emphasizes the alchemical principle of "friendship" between substances, arguing that the Elixir works most effectively on metals that are already nearly perfect.</summary>

# A Closing Discourse and the End of this Art.

I have now given you, in my aforementioned writings and teachings, a clear and perfect treatise / which one names or calls a **Mirror of Alchemy** / wherein there appears, just as in a mirror, the meaning and secret of the entire art of <term>alchemy</term> <note>original: *Alchymen*.</note> / in which all <term>philosophers</term> <note>In alchemical literature, "philosophers" almost always refers to the ancient and medieval masters of the "Great Work," such as Hermes Trismegistus or Geber.</note> agree with one another / and as the treatise of the **Mirror of Alchemy** explains and interprets the end / therefore I was not mistaken to call it a treatise / but rather it reveals itself as a mirror / although it is to be considered in itself for learning the right art / yet it covers its face only from the uninitiated <note>original: *unbekandten*, meaning those who have not been "introduced" to the secret terminology.</note> / but to the wise / it testifies very beautifully and subtly to the right art : Just as anyone / who looks at themselves in a mirror / and therein beholds and recognizes their own figure / which then looks back at them again.

So it is also with the **Mirror of Alchemy** / if one diligently beholds and reads through it / then there shines out from it more than a subtle and beautiful art of alchemy / which is so beautiful and subtle / and also so worthy / that it enlightens the knowledge <note>original: *Erkäntnüß*.</note> of a heartfelt and subtle <term>alchemist</term> <note>original: *Alchymisten*.</note> / so that he can see the whole truth / naked and uncovered therein / and for the sake of the worthiness of the art / we add for assistance the following figure or characters.

->JESUS MARIA.<-

# A BRIEF PREFACE.

*Because the most highly honored and most valiant King Alfonso the Fifth <note>original: "Quintus". While the text identifies him as the fifth, the historical King Alfonso "the Wise" associated with these translations is Alfonso X. The discrepancy may be a scribal error or a specific regional numbering.</note>, by the grace of God King of Castile and León, son of the Lord King Servandus <note>likely a reference to King Ferdinand III, known as San Fernando</note> and the Lady Queen Beatrice, wished to commend his name to eternal memory: for this reason, he strove to restore to the memory of his successors the sciences that had been entirely neglected during the times of his predecessors. Among many other things, he took great care to have this book, titled the **KEY OF WISDOM** <note>original: "CLAVIS SAPIENTIAE"</note>, diligently translated from the Arabic language into his own native Castilian by one of his squires. This **BOOK** is divided into three chapters, and none of them is complete without the others. For the first requires the second and third, and the third requires the first and second. The first chapter, therefore, deals with the explanation of the Higher and Lower Elements, as well as the nature of equal and unequal things, and their mutual conversion and generation. The second chapter deals with the generation of mineral bodies, both natural and artificial. The third deals with the generation of plants and animals, and the binding of the Spirit with the plant, and also of the animal soul with the living creature, etc.*

## CHAPTER I.

->*On the explanation of the Higher and Lower Elements, and also of unequal natures: and their mutual conversion, and of Generation.*<-

Let us praise GOD at the beginning, who is the Inspector of all things, nor is there anything that can be hidden from him. For He himself is bound <note>original: "alligatus"</note> to his creatures through his word, and yet separated from them insofar as he transcends them. For I do not think that he created anything similar to himself, or equal: And among the great benefits of God, the greatest is this: that he bound our body with the most subtle of all Elements, namely the soul <note>original: "anima"</note>, which sees hidden things, just as it has already seen them, provided that the virtues of the body itself 
<margin>,,</margin> do not predominate over it. For the more the 
<margin>,,</margin> powers of the body itself are strengthened, the 
<margin>,,</margin> more the virtues of the Soul itself must necessarily 
<margin>,,</margin> be weakened: And the more we 
<margin>,,</margin> weaken <note>literally "thin out" or "attenuate"</note> the body, the more the 
<margin>,,</margin> insights of the soul itself are refined. And for this reason our Master *Bellonus the Philosopher* <note>Likely a reference to Apollonius of Tyana, often called "Balinas" in Arabic sources from which this text was translated.</note> said: *Place your light in a clear glass vessel.* And it is known that all the wisdom of this world revolves around these three things, namely: around the binding of a corporal soul with a corporal soul, and of a spiritual soul with a corporal one, and of a spiritual one with a spiritual one. But the binding of a corporal soul with a corporal one is closer and easier than the spiritual with the spiritual. Regarding that third type, the ancient Sages wished to write very little. For they said that the intellect could not reach the knowledge of it, unless its nature was like its [the soul's] nature, and its birth was also like its birth. Therefore, what is it that all the ancient sages said in harmony regarding diversity? That that which is above, is like that which—

# The Key of Wisdom.

...that which is below is as that which is above, and vice versa: And all that is **Subtle** is in the **Gross**, and the **Gross** comes from the **Subtle**. <note>original: "illud quod est inferius... omne subtile est in Grosso"</note> And every composition of the whole world—whether of the **greater** <note>the macrocosm or the universe</note>, the **middle** <note>the mesocosm</note>, or the **lesser** <note>the microcosm or man</note>—is a single composition. And you should know that the **binding** <note>original: "alligamentum"; referring to the structural link or "glue" of reality</note> of all worldly things is like the **binding of Number**, namely composed of Units, Tens, Hundreds, and Thousands. For from the digits is generated the first rank, as when we say One, Two, Three, etc.; which, if they are gathered together, constitute a **ten** <note>original: "denarium"</note>. Similarly, if you say 10, 20, 30, 40: from these numbers gathered together, the number **One Hundred** is produced. This same principle can be seen in the hundreds and the thousands. For since number is nothing other than the binding of one thing with another, it is manifest that the unit of number does not itself count as a number <note>In ancient and medieval philosophy, "One" was often considered the source or principle of numbers rather than a number itself.</note>.

Therefore, when we take the **Binary** <term>the number two; the first true number representing duality</term>, which is the first number, and divide it into two equal parts, it is clear that its other part is and exists as a unit; if you wish to add this unit to the binary, the **Ternary** <note>the number three</note> will result. If, however, you wish to double the Binary, the **Quaternary** <note>the number four</note> is born from it; if you add a unit to this Quaternary, it will produce the **Quinary** <note>the number five</note> for you. If you then add the **Trinary** <note>the number three</note> to that same Quaternary again, you will receive the **Septenary** <note>the number seven</note>, which, with a unit added to it, will procreate the **Octonary** <note>the number eight</note> for you. By adding a unit to this again, you will find the **Novenary** <note>the number nine</note>; but if you add the Binary, it will procreate the **Denary** <note>the number ten</note> for you. In that same way, Hundreds are procreated from Tens, and Thousands from the hundreds.

One day, my Master **Bellonus the Philosopher** <note>Likely a reference to Apollonius of Tyana, a famous sage of antiquity</note> called me and said: "Come now, Son, I hope you are a man of special intellect, and that you might even reach the supreme joy of **wisdom** <note>original: "sapientiæ"</note>. I will therefore question you, and you shall answer me." And I said

This Light, however, contained the first creature within its own hollow sphere. Of this nature—that is, the nature of the creature—the creature was of heat and motion, from which it is clear that the first was of cold and stillness. And because they were brought close to one another, the heat struck the cold, and the cold constrained itself, condensing its own being. For one part of heat tempered itself with an equal part of moisture, and from this tempering came the nature of "heat and moisture." Its place, as we said before, was midway between the place of heat and of moisture. And because, as we stated previously, the nature of moisture is composed of one part heat and one part moisture <note>original: "humiditatis"; this appears to be a scribal error for "frigiditatis" (coldness), as moisture is defined above as a mix of heat and cold.</note> equal to it, it follows that the nature of "heat and moisture" will consist of one part coldness and three parts heat. In the same way, the nature of "coldness and moisture" is aggregated from the nature of coldness and the nature of moisture equally. And because half of the nature of moisture is heat and half is coldness, it follows that the nature of "coldness and moisture" consists of three parts coldness and one part heat.

Now, therefore, we have—above the <term>sphere</term> <note>In the Aristotelian-Ptolemaic worldview, the universe was composed of nested concentric spheres, each governed by different spiritual and physical laws.</note> of the first nature which we mentioned before—four ordered spheres. And because motion from above to below is not only opposed by motion from below to above, but also because—as we say—one part of heat, which had not mixed with the Nature of coldness to generate moisture, remained below, mixed with coldness itself. This is the classical Aristotelian principle of *horror vacui*, the idea that nature will always fill empty space with matter.</note>, a certain part of coldness exists in equal measure in the place of that heat which descends below.

It is clear, therefore, how these Spheres were connected to one another. For the lowest was the **Sphere of coldness and dryness** <note>original: "Sphær frigiditatis & siccitatis"; this corresponds to the element of Earth.</note>, in which there is nothing of heat. After this, however, follows the **Sphere of coldness and moisture** <note>The element of Water.</note>, in which there are three parts of coldness and one part of heat. Then follows the **Sphere of Equality**, which is the **Sphere of the Soul**, half of which is of the nature of heat and the other half of coldness. Above this is the **Sphere of Sensation**, which is of heat and moisture, half of which is of the nature of heat and the other half of the nature of moisture.

Now, we have already said that half of the nature of moisture consists of the nature of heat, and the other half of the nature of coldness. Therefore, of this Sphere, three parts are of the Nature of heat, and one part is of the Nature of Coldness. But the supreme Sphere, which comes after it, is entirely of the nature of heat, nor is there anything in it [of coldness...]

We say that even granted that quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum"; mercury</note> and sulfur are the natural principles of mineral bodies before they harden <note>original: "congelationem"</note>, it would still be impossible for quicksilver and sulfur to be generated from those mineral bodies after they have hardened. An example of this is the composition of Soap. For if one takes water extracted from ash <note>lye</note> and oil with certain other things, and boils them in a specific way, Soap is produced from them. Now, sulfur was originally water, being cold and moist in nature. Afterwards it was converted into Air, which is hot and moist; and then into fire, which is hot and dry. This example is clear in plants. We know that the generation of a plant occurs in water with fine soil, as we said before; and yet, if we simply took water and soil, we could never grow a plant. And this is the reason why other animals do not discern <note>possess the power of reason or judgment</note> as **MAN** does.

The composition of the human body, however, consists in a certain commingling of equal natures with unequal ones. The nature of quality consists in the composition of the human being in two parts, one of which is an apparent or extrinsic equality, and the other is a certain intrinsic one. The intrinsic equality is the nature of the soul itself, of which we spoke before. Apparent equality, however, consists in the equal composition of the body itself and the four humors <note>the four bodily fluids thought to determine health and temperament</note>, which are: <term>Blood</term> <note>original: *Sanguis*</note>, which is hot and moist, belonging to the nature of air; and <term>Choler</term> <note>Yellow bile; original: *Cholera*</note>, hot and dry, belonging to the nature of fire; and <term>Phlegm</term> <note>original: *Phlegma*</note>, which is cold and moist by nature, belonging to the nature of water; and <term>Melancholy</term> <note>Black bile; original: *Melancholia*</note>, which is cold and dry, belonging to the nature of earth. And this is the following figure.

# THE OPINION OF THE 
# MOST DISTINGUISHED MASTER GERHARD DORN, &c.
## Interpreter of the works of Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus Paracelsus, the famous 16th-century Swiss physician and alchemist</note>, concerning the Stone of the Philosophers.

A metal should be reduced into a powder <note>original: "calcem" – a "calx" is the crumbly residue left after a metal has been heated or chemically broken down</note> using common mercury, and it should be added to an equal portion of quicksilver <note>original: "Mercurii vivi," literally "living mercury"</note> in a sublimation vessel. Let it remain there together until they merge into a single mass. Then, let the mercury be drawn upward through heat <note>original: "sublimetur" – sublimation is the process of heating a substance into vapor and then cooling it back into a solid</note> and ground down, repeating this process as many times as necessary until the mass begins to flow like wax when it is gently brought near the flame of a candle. Once this is observed, let it be placed in a digestion vessel <note>term: <term>Digestorium</term> — a vessel used to provide constant, gentle heat for a long period, simulating the warmth of an animal's stomach</note> for the appropriate amount of time, and the whole will be transformed into quicksilver. This is called the Mercury of the Metals and of the Philosophers, which has been sought by many until now, but discovered by very few indeed, etc.

### II.

# THE TREATISE OF ARISTOTLE THE ALCHEMIST TO ALEXANDER THE GREAT, CONCERNING THE PHILOSOPHERS’ STONE.

->Formerly written down, and collected by a certain Christian Philosopher.<-

## A BRIEF DISCOURSE.

Having invoked the Name of Christ, I have considered that in the works of nature—which are to be brought to completion through the service of art <note>In this context, "art" refers to the alchemical skill used to perfect or accelerate natural processes</note>—many people work in vain. This is because they understand the books of the Philosophers only according to the "outer shell" <note>original: "secundum corticem" — a common medieval metaphor for the literal or surface-level meaning of a text, as opposed to its hidden "pith" or truth</note> of the words. Consequently, they suffer countless losses of their wealth and property. Therefore, in this treatise, I will provide a certain figure <note>A symbolic diagram or illustration</note>, intending to explain it in part, just as I found it in a certain book that was an explanation of Aristotle’s *Meteorology* <note>original: "Meteororum" — Aristotle's scientific work on natural phenomena; here, the author claims to have found alchemical secrets hidden within it</note>. He sent this to ALEXANDER in the tranquility of peace regarding this figure. It says: "Take the animal and vegetable Stone." For fire lies hidden under the water, which is white and clear, and earth under the air, whose greenness is converted into whiteness. Let us not seek other elements besides earth and water: for **AIR** and **FIRE** are included within their own merits and effects.

This **SERPENT** <note>original: "SERPENS"; in alchemy, this often represents Mercury or the volatile "spirit" of the matter</note> is composed of a vile <note>common or inexpensive</note> material, which is led here and there in the chariot of its vessel by a fourfold revolution of the natures <note>likely referring to the cycling through the four elements: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth</note>. But let it be closed securely, where evaporations occur between two humid and hot signs for 40 days, until they are converted into the black water of nature. This is the sign of the perfect conception of both [the male and female principles], of which, once the Moisture has totally evaporated, nothing remains except that its **EARTH** be refreshed with its own water to a third part. This is the sign of perfect whiteness, which afterwards, with a double proportion of its water, will be converted at various times into true water. And this is the end of the first operation, and the beginning of the goal of all Philosophers.

You should know, however, that this **SERPENT** can be "weakened" <note>or corrupted/made defective</note> in a fourfold way by the so-called **4 WHEELS** of the Elements. First, in the "head"—that is, in the selection of its material—for a thing is rarely perfected without the established order of **NATURE**. And this occurs when nature is sufficiently capable: it should be perfectly balanced in temperament, healthy, flowing, and of a sanguine complexion <note>indicating a vigorous, red, or life-giving quality</note>, not black, thin, or even hard.

Once this **ONE** <note>the unified starting material</note> is placed in its spherical tomb <note>the round glass flask or "Philosopher's Egg"</note>, closed on all sides, it is observed thus: If it does not dissolve itself in the vessel like butter, reaching a certain whiteness swimming on the surface within seven days, and if a rarefaction of the matter occurs and heat appears in that part, the work begun will achieve little. This is because the internal effect is revealed through signs and similarities appearing on the outside.

You should have another pot continuously boiling in a bath <note>original: "balneo"; likely a water bath or "Bain-marie" used for gentle, indirect heat</note>, and of the same matter and nature, pouring in the distilled water from it to dissolve your **EGG** <note>original: "OVUM"; the alchemical vessel</note>. In this way, the materials can be properly liquefied by art—not by force, but by a spherical motion and continuous, moderate heat, with the vessel closed as I have taught. For it is certain that our earthy substance cannot be dissolved without the proper and conforming water. Let the vessel not be long,

The material should fill only a third of the vessel, which must be well-sealed with a concave <note>original: "concavo"; hollowed or bowl-shaped</note> glass lid, rather than a flat one. The glass should be fashioned rounder at the bottom than at the top; it should not be very thick, but clear and clean. It should sit in a bed of horse dung <note>original: "fimi equini"; horse manure was a standard alchemical heat source, providing a steady, gentle, "living" warmth similar to an incubator</note> up to two-thirds of its height. 

Only one part of the vessel should remain free of the "smoke" <note>vapors or steam</note>. You must watch to ensure that the smoke or vapor does not reach the lid of the vessel too evenly; the lid itself should be kept exposed to the open air. This is because sometimes external vapors can cool the upper part of the vessel, causing an unwanted internal change <note>original: "alterationis"</note>.

The **Manure-bed** <note>original: "Fimarium"; a specialized furnace or pit filled with dung</note> should be built between strong walls in a circular shape, which allows the heat to be better preserved. This place should be visited often to check for "unnatural burnings" <note>overheating that might scorch the delicate matter</note>, and it must be situated where neither wind nor outside air can cause harm. 

Note how much care is required for the distillation of the material: it requires the same "regime of fire" <note>level of heat intensity</note> as was used during the **putrefaction** <note>the stage of the work where the matter is broken down or "rotted" into a black mass</note>. It must be distilled in such a way that no **OIL** appears. Oil is produced only by an error in the "concoction" <note>the slow cooking or digestion</note> of the matter. Therefore, if oil appears, there is no hope for a perfect distillation, only total loss.

The remedy for this problem is as follows: as soon as oil begins to distill, remove the **Alembic** <note>the "helmet" or still-head of the distilling apparatus</note>. Return the matter to the previously described order of putrefaction, mixing it with the water that was extracted from the material. With a modest fire, this "infirmity" <note>defect or sickness of the matter</note> will be cured, though it will take a longer time, as it is necessary to putrefy this...

# Concerning the Philosophers’ Stone #
## Z 3 ##

...[perfe]ction <note>original: "ctionem"; likely completing "perfectionem" or "distillationem"</note> should be maintained for eight continuous days, and then let it be distilled again, as said above; and therefore, advice should be taken in case of a failure <note>original: "in defectu consilium"; referring to troubleshooting or correcting the process if it goes wrong</note>.

For it is held as a general rule that in this work only **TWO ELEMENTS** are ever seen: namely, **EARTH** and **WATER**. For Fire is contained within the Earth, and Air within the Water. Therefore, Aristotle says in his *Secrets to Alexander* <note>The "Secretum Secretorum," a highly influential medieval text of occult wisdom falsely attributed to the philosopher Aristotle</note>: "Perfect the earth with its celestial water, and the whole work is perfected."

**THIS EARTH** is the **EARTH OF THE FIFTH ESSENCE** <term>Fifth Essence: Also known as the *Quintessence*, this was believed to be the purest, most refined form of matter, transcending the four physical elements and possessing miraculous healing properties</term>, because it is reduced to that specific degree. For the Fifth Essence in **EVERY THING** is the ultimate goal of Nature’s operation and power; because, by its own nature, it cannot be led to any further external stage. In that degree resides **ALL FORCE AND NATURE** that can be possessed by any sublunary body <note>Sublunary body: Any physical object on Earth, existing beneath the "sphere of the moon" and thus subject to change and decay</note>, because its nature stops being in the fourth degree, but it takes the fifth from beyond the Elements.

Understand now **ONE SUPREME SECRET**: That every Fifth Essence is, by itself, a preservative of health for any body; and it holds within itself every power and effect for any thing of the same temperament <note>original: "complexionis"; referring to the balance of humors or qualities in a substance</note> and condition, and not for another.

Just as the Fifth Essence of a poison brings health only to poisonous things, and so it is with others: **THUS**, the Essence of metals heals every infirmity of metals. From this, it is concluded that the science of the **PHILOSOPHERS’ STONE** is **TRUE** and infallible, lacking all falsehood. Secondly: that whoever seeks this Science to heal the infirmities of metals labors in vain, seeks in vain, and finds neither end nor success <note>original: "salutem"</note> unless they do so through their Fifth Essence.

Whence, from the earth artificially reduced to its Fifth Essence, and the Water likewise, and from these combined with one another, **PERFECTION** arises, through which all Philosophers...

# On the Philosopher’s Stone #
# Page 369 #

The **Fifth Essence** <note>original: "Q. Essentiam"</note> brings itself back by its own work, and not by the distillation of hands. And so the said Water must be kept continually covered, lest it breathe and the **Flower** <note>The "Flower" refers to the volatile spirit or the most subtle part of the substance that can easily evaporate if not sealed</note> escape. And this I once proved to have been the error of a certain work begun by me: Therefore I took new water of the same nature, virtue, and grace, and I perfected what I desired.

Now it remains to speak of the errors occurring in the work, by which it happens that many deviate from the right path. It must be noted, therefore, that the **first Error** lies in the discontinuation and adversity of the Fires in the same work, according to the same Greek <note>Likely referring to Aristotle or another Greek authority in the alchemical tradition</note>. For not only the heat, but the quality of the color must be attended to: For a hot and moist fire, as in a bath, and a dry fire, [as in a furnace], have different effects. For one helps toward the perfection of the dissolution, such as the **Horse’s Belly** <term>Horse’s Belly: *Venter Equinus*, a traditional alchemical term for a heap of decomposing horse manure, which provided a steady, gentle, moist heat for "digesting" a substance over a long period</term>: The other fire, however, possesses a different dissolution and causes an alteration in the Matter. Therefore the **True Philosophers** say that in a perfect work there must be **One Fire**, **One Regimen**, **One Vessel**, and thus in all things there will be equality of the work and harmony of the whole. This **Fire**, however, must be moderated according to the stage of the operation, so that until the **Whiteness** <note>original: "albedinem"; the *Albedo*, or second major stage of the Great Work, signifying purification</note> it is always slow, just like the natural heat of a man, or the heat of an Egg being hatched by the mother in her nest; from whence [comes] the matter of the Stone, which is man’s **fourth digestion** <term>Fourth Digestion: In medieval physiology, the final stage of the digestive process where nutrients are fully transformed into the substance of the body's organs and limbs</term>, composed of the four natures.

In the first work and its true decay <note>original: "putrefactione"</note>, the true essence comes forth into its own **Fifth Essence**, which is the beginning of our perfect work and **Mastery** <term>Mastery: *Magisterium*, the successful completion of the alchemical process or the creation of the Philosopher's Stone itself</term>. And therefore, according to what the Philosopher <note>Aristotle</note> says: The beginning of the corruption of **One** is the generation of another unto a different nature and effect: Whence the aforesaid matter must be so dissolved in continuous heat, which heat shall have **Three** things within itself: namely, moisture from itself, and heat without dryness,

...and the reason of its compacted matter: And if any of these things should be lacking, it will not have a successful effect, unless one works more cautiously and subtly.

The second **ERROR** concerns the matter from which the Stone is brought to its origin or action. For the Stone <note>original: *Lapis*; the Philosopher's Stone, the goal of the alchemical Great Work</note> must be selected from a healthy vein after perfect digestion, found through young people who are unspent, prosperous, and healthy, of middle age or younger, and of a sanguine temperament <note>The "sanguine" temperament was associated with blood, air, and a cheerful, active disposition in medieval medicine</note>. For the gluttonous, the greedy, the lecherous, the old, or the sick cannot generate a useful Stone, because of the hidden virtues of Nature, which cannot be attained through powers of that kind. And because our **STONE** is likened to the **Greater WORLD** <note>original: *Majori MUNDO*; the Macrocosm or the universe as a whole</note>, its composition cannot fail in any of its nature, because of the incineration of the entire completion.

The third **ERROR** is in the **VESSEL**: For the Vessel ought to be spherical, and entirely round at the bottom with proportional sides, with its "head" <note>the top part or neck of the flask</note> almost twice as large, and a height of nearly one cubit <note>a traditional unit of length, roughly 18 inches or the length of a forearm</note>. Likewise, it ought to be made of glass and not be porous, well-sealed with its suitable lute <note>original: *luto*; a specialized paste or clay used by alchemists to airtightly seal glass equipment</note>; but this shall be done in the beginning after the evaporation of the matter in its perfect selection after its perfect generation, as is said above.

It should be noted that the evaporation of the matter should not last longer than its heat remains, which sometimes used to last for three hours. Hence we perceive that nothing else is to be done in this work, except that the vessel with the matter stands in some secret place with a cloth placed over it, so that no dust enters, and any accidental moisture from the cloth is entirely expelled from the vessel. And this work is done for two reasons: first, because of the sudden change of nature; second, because of the expulsion of accidental moistures, which would be the cause of the extinction of the **LIVING MATTER** <note>original: *MATERIÆ VIVACIS*</note> in our **STONE**, and the incineration of the same.

### Concerning the Philosopher's Stone

The **Fourth Error** will sometimes occur in distillation, when the material is distilled more than is necessary, or is "exalted" <note>original: *exaltatur*; to raise or refine a substance's potency or spiritual state through alchemical processes</note> too much. For in the **Water** there are specifically three things: **Spirit, Soul, and Tincture** <note>These represent the three fundamental principles of alchemical substances: the volatile aspect (spirit), the vitalizing principle (soul), and the coloring or transformative power (tincture)</note>. For the Spirit and Soul do not penetrate except through a certain corrosive force, although in various distillations the power and **Nature** are entirely weakened. And if the water should be turbid and not clear, it rectifies itself without distillation, and whatever remains at the bottom should be cast away to the earth.

The **Fifth Error** is in the rectification of the **Earth**, and this shall be done little by little, so that as often as it is soaked, it is dried out just as many times. Hence, there are three parts of water to one part of its Earth, and sometimes more, if it is required for perfect dissolution. And the perfect dissolution of this work is its most perfect **Quintessence** <note>original: *quinta Essentia*; the "fifth element" or the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance, believed to have universal healing powers</note>, possessing within itself every medicinal power and a wonderful fragrance, full of all sweetness.

There are **Three Signs** of perfect dissolution. First, that it be true Water in itself without dregs; second, that it be milky on the surface; third, that it have a honey-like flavor and sweetness on the tongue. **Note Well**: This aforementioned material congeals itself with hot and dry fire, and dissolves itself with hot and moist fire. And this **Water** is permanent and perpetual, which on account of its wonderful virtues possesses all the power of stones. Therefore, it is named by the name of all Stones. This is **Quicksilver** <note>original: *Argentum Vivum*; mercury</note>, **Sulfur**, **Orpiment** <note>original: *Auripigmentum*; a golden-yellow arsenic mineral</note>, and it is called by infinite other names; and yet none of these is present in its literal nature, but rather in its **Virtue** <note>In alchemy, "virtue" refers to the inherent power or essential quality of a substance rather than its physical chemical makeup</note>. For it is Quicksilver because it possesses perfect virtue and life within itself; and it is incombustible Sulfur, and therefore it draws every sign with it according to its primary meaning. This is because a sign takes its naming from what follows after, regarding its principal meaning.

### Aristotle’s Treatise on Alchemy

<note>Though attributed to Aristotle, this text is part of a "pseudo-Aristotelian" tradition of alchemical writings popular in the Middle Ages and Renaissance.</note>

The **sixth and final error** lies in the continuation and projection of the work: For if there were any discontinuity in the heat, in the vessel, or in the timing, the incineration of the work would follow. The timing is equal—namely, 40 days for **putrefaction** <note>original: *putrefactio*; the stage of "death" or breaking down where the matter turns black</note>, 40 days for **whiteness**, 40 days for <unclear>redness</unclear> <note>The OCR is clipped here, but alchemical tradition usually follows the sequence of Black, White, then Red (Rubedo)</note>, and 40 days for **perfect dissolution**, provided that the management of the fire is duly moderated and applied.

In the first period, it is called the **Stone that is not a Stone** <note>original: *Lapis non Lapis*; a common alchemical riddle signifying that the substance has the weight of a stone but the properties of a spirit</note>; in the second, the **Stone**; in the third, **Quicksilver**; and in the fourth, the **Ruby**. These names are given by Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of alchemy</note>, and in part by Aristotle and Morienus <note>Morienus was a legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist known for teaching the secrets of the Stone to the King Khalid ibn Yazid</note>.

The sign in putrefaction is a thinness along with supreme **Blackness**. The sign of the distillation or calcination of the Stone is dryness with incineration. The sign of **whitening** <note>original: *dealbatio*; the stage where the matter is purified</note> is that it should be shining like white lime without any mixed blackness. The sign of **dissolution** is that nothing remains undissolved, but the whole becomes like a very clear, **Stagnant Water**, without dregs. However, if it happens otherwise, the dregs should be cast out. But if the dregs are pale and not like "nourished wool," not only should they enter our work, but the aforementioned dregs, along with the aforementioned water of our Stone, are similarly valuable when distilled for **Medicines** to cure **All Bodily Infirmities**; therefore, the dregs should not be cast away.

The **PROJECTION** <note>The final act of alchemical transformation, where a small amount of the "Stone" is cast upon a larger mass of molten base metal to transform it into gold or silver</note> of our Stone is such that first, one part of the said **Blessed Stone**, congealed in hot ashes, is projected upon 10 parts of heated common **Mercury**, so that the said Mercury is thus incorporated with the Stone; once fixed, it is projected upon 100 parts. And if it is projected twice, it is effective over a thousand; and if a third time, over a million; indeed, over any metal, however imperfect, according to the quality of the Medicine,

## I I I.

# THE FOLLOWING IS AN EPISTLE TO THE MOST REVEREND LORD HERMANN, Archbishop of Cologne, regarding the Philosopher’s Stone, by a certain monk of the Benedictine Order, etc., reviewing the short works of Plato and ARNOLD of Villanova.

Know, most reverend and serene Prince, that few attain this art in truth, because they never strive toward the proper end. Since, however, *Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of Lights* <note>original Latin: *Omne Datum Optimum, & Omne Donum Perfectum Desursum sit à Patre Luminum*—a quotation from the Epistle of James 1:17.</note>, as witnessed by James, and the Spirit blows only where it wills: Truly know this, that it is a gift of God, granted to the sons of God and to those devoted to the art, namely to Catholic and Evangelical men. Therefore, do not wonder, O illustrious **PRELATE** <term>prelate: a high-ranking member of the clergy, in this case, the Archbishop</term>, that this Art is contained in **One Single thing**, requires nothing else, and is perfected in **One Single Vessel** and by **One Single operation**, which operation is called the perfect **Sublimation** <term>sublimation: the alchemical process of vaporizing a substance and then condensing it, used to purify the matter</term> of the Philosophers, through which our **STONE** is truly made, as the Philosophers clearly teach. This **STONE** is indeed a **STONE**, and yet not a stone, and it is Mercury and Sulphur; in which the four **ELEMENTS** <term>elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water, which the alchemist seeks to bring into perfect harmony</term> are so proportioned that almost none is contrary to the other. And know, O Prince, that there is no Mercury nor Sulphur so perfect as that which is found in the bodies of the **SUN** <note>original: *SOLIS*, referring to Gold</note> and the **MOON** <note>original: *LUNAE*, referring to Silver</note>; and the Philosophers call our Stone the **SUN**;

<header>Epistle on the Philosopher’s Stone</header>

This is not the **COMMON SUN**, but our **SUN** <note>original Latin: *SOL VULGARIS* and *SOL nofter*</note>. And they call it the **MOON**, and yet it is also not the Common Moon, but our Moon, or that of the **PHILOSOPHERS**; and they have called it **SULPHUR** and **MERCURY** <term>Sulphur and Mercury: in alchemy, these are not the chemical elements we know today, but "philosophical" principles representing the active/solar and passive/lunar forces</term>, and this is according to how it is changed through different and various Operations.

And know, O renowned **PRELATE** and most illustrious **PRELATE**, that when this is declared to you, you shall know the whole, and you shall know the mind of all the Philosophers: For it takes those diverse names according to its diverse conversions, namely into Water and Earth, Air and black, white, and red dust.

And note, that in its perfect sublimation and operation only two **ELEMENTS** are seen, namely Earth and Water: But under the earth **FIRE** is contained, and under the Water, **AIR**, which two—namely Fire and Air—are invisible, except under earth and water.

And note, O Prince, when the philosophical **sublimation** <term>sublimation: the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then condenses, used here metaphorically for purification</term> takes place, then the most perfect body is taken and placed in the fire of the Philosophers, for the month of the Philosophers; then, in time, that Body is moistened and emits a certain bloody sweat after its **putrefaction** <term>putrefaction: the stage of the work where the material decays and turns black, also called the Nigredo</term> and **mortification**. I speak of the **HEAVENLY DEW**, which is indeed called the **MERCURY** of the Philosophers, or Permanent Water, Living Water; I speak of the Water which, by leaving its body, kills it, and by entering it, brings it to life, turns it black, and turns it white, according to the Gospel:

> Unless a grain of wheat falling into the earth dies, it remains alone. <note>original Latin: *Nisi granum frumenti cadens in terram mortuum fuerit, ipsum solum manet*—from the Gospel of John 12:24.</note>

Whence the Philosophers say, our **STONE** is one, and our **STONE** kills itself, decays itself, and brings itself back to life, and washes and whitens itself, and has within itself all necessary things, and needs the help of nothing else.

And note, O you glorious Prince, that the Water which exits from the Body is called the **SOUL** and the **SPIRIT** of the body.

And then the earth is said to be empty, yet having fire within itself—and that Water is called the **Mercury of the Philosophers**, and **Permanent Water**, and **Air**. And note, O **PRELATE**, that when our Stone emits that sweat <note>original: *sudorem*, referring to the liquid produced during the chemical reaction</note>, then the earth remains at the bottom black, like **Pitch**: And while by often subliming <term>subliming: the process of heating a substance to a gas and back to a solid to purify it</term> it falls back upon it, its water whitens it, and converts it into a most white and most subtle powder. This white powder is called the **White Stone** or the **Moon**. And above all note, that there are three principal Colors, namely **BLACK**, **WHITE**, and **RED**. I call it **Black**, when first the heat acting upon the moist body generates blackness, as is clearly evident from the Philosopher <note>likely referring to Aristotle, often called "The Philosopher" in medieval texts</note>. And heat acting upon the dry body, with a true washing, generates whiteness: And heat acting upon that whiteness generates a yellow color <note>original: *citrinitatem*, the "Citrinitas" or yellowing stage of the alchemical work</note>. You will understand all of this in what follows through the touch of your hands, and in all the writings of the Philosophers who write truly of our Stone.

And note, that while our Stone has been turned into white, it is called the **Moon**: And when, through the continuation of the work and the increase of the Fire, it is converted into red, it is called the **Sun**. And this Stone of ours is not the common Moon or Sun, but it is the **Philosophical Moon** or **Sun** <note>original uses the symbol ☉ for the Sun</note>, sublimated and glorified, and brought to such great subtlety that it has the power of converting Mercury and all metallic bodies into **GOLD** or **SILVER**, more perfect than any found in mines. This is testified to fully enough in the works written below, namely those of **PLATO** <note>referring to alchemical texts traditionally attributed to the Greek philosopher Plato</note> and **ARNOLD** <note>Arnold of Villanova, a famed 13th-century physician and alchemist</note>.

### Concerning the Philosopher's Stone

Indeed, they return to those things from which they were created, just as to their first origin. But the turning around of those circles <note>original: *circulorum*, referring to the cyclical nature of the elements transforming into one another</note> is by no means completed until they are reduced to the first matter. Once reduced to the first matter, they are neither seen nor touched, except as **Water** & **Earth** only. **Air**, indeed, and **Fire** are never seen, except that their virtues are known—that is, they are perceived by the senses—within the elements of **Water** and **Earth**. And unless these four elements are so joined together, they accomplish nothing. When they are joined, however, they constitute the **Medicine** which we seek.

Know therefore, all of you, that there is **No True Tincture** <term>Tincture: in alchemy, a substance capable of transforming or "coloring" other materials, often used as a synonym for the Stone or Elixir</term> except from our **Air**, because Nature is not improved except within its own nature. Therefore, do not lose your money in vain, nor bring sadness to your hearts by seeking another Stone. For **Our Stone** is **One**, and its **Rule** <term>regimen: the specific method of heating and managing the chemical process</term> is One, and its **Arrangement** is One. 

Moreover, our Stone is **Permanent Water**, pure, shining, and clear, having a celestial color, and more honorable than **Gold**: because without it, our Water is not improved. Yet no transforming poison <note>original: *venenum*, used here in the alchemical sense of a potent, transformative substance or "tincture" rather than a harmful toxin</note> is generated without the **SUN** <note>original: *SOLE*, referring to gold or the solar principle</note> and its shadow. Whoever strives to transform without these accomplishes **NOTHING**.

The **Rule** of our Stone is to cook it continuously in its vessel, and to dissolve it by cooking with a light fire; then to sublimate <term>sublimate: to heat a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again, used here to represent the "ascent" of the spirit</term> the dissolved matter into the **Air**, and again to condense the whole into the **earth**. Its **Arrangement** is first to blacken it, and afterwards to whiten it with a more intense fire. Once whitened, it is to be burned <note>original: *incinerare*, to reduce to a dry state or ash through heat</note> with a second portion of its Water, and turned into a true **RED** <note>original: *RuBEUM*, the final Rubedo stage</note> with great heat.

Therefore, join our **Red Servant**, purified from all impurity, with his **Fragrant Wife**, purified from all defilement, and they will bring forth the Art for you. Place them in a vessel over a light fire,

...and cook it until it becomes a thickened broth <note>original: *brodium saginatum*, referring to a rich, dense liquid state in the flask</note>. It is necessary, therefore, to repeatedly sublime <term>sublimare: to heat a substance until it vapors and then solidifies again, used here to purify the "spirit"</term> both vapors so that the whole becomes endowed with life. In the air, then, when you wish, join the intention conversely, until the work is perfected.

<term>Take:</term> 2 parts of the said powder, and cast them upon 100 parts of the purified **Male and Female** <note>referring to the active and passive principles, often Sulfur and Mercury</note> (that is, upon 100 parts of the remaining first subject), and having been prepared as described above, place them again in the glass house. ## PROLOGUE TO THE SONS AND BROTHERS OF DOCTRINE II.

Concerning the venerable antiquity, uncorrupted truth, singular nobility, and wondrous excellence of the Divine, Magical, and Celestial chemical art—joined as it is with miraculous and ineffable fruits—I have decided, most select Brothers and Sons of the Hermetic doctrine, that it is not necessary to deliver a long-winded speech in this place. This is because, in our own time, there are already many laudatory <note>original: "ἐγκωμιαστικὰ" (encomiastic); refers to speeches or writings intended to highly praise a subject</note> writings by learned men available concerning the praises of this most useful and pleasant study, to which I wish to refer you for your present knowledge.

After the time of HERMES TRISMEGISTUS <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the founder of alchemy and Hermetic philosophy</note>, this Art flourished among the Egyptians, Arabs, Greeks, and others, as evidenced by the names of nearly six hundred Philosophers who wrote about the Philosopher’s Stone <term>Philosopher’s Stone: The legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and providing the Elixir of Life</term>. They left the mysteries of the Chemical art to us as their posterity, though they kept them veiled in infinite parables and hidden under obscure coverings. In the interval of the age preceding this one, our Monarch and Master of Mysteries <note>original: "Mysteriarcha"</note>, PHILIPPUS THEOPHRASTUS Paracelsus, etc., flourished in Germany. He planted, expanded once more, and illuminated this chemical truth and art in writings that are more than divine—though they are not accessible to everyone, but only to the sons of doctrine. He applied this art to the most desperate diseases, such as Leprosy, Gout <note>original: "Podagra"</note>, Paralysis, and others...
